title: California football coach arrested after students make disturbing discovery at school
summary: The Tracy Unified School District placed the educator and football coach, Jeffrey Pribble, on leave as separate criminal and district investigations continue.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A high school football coach in California was arrested Friday after students discovered a cellphone secretly recording them while they were changing inside a campus locker room, police said.
The phone allegedly belonged to Jeffrey Pribble, a 48-year-old teacher at Tracy High School, located east of San Francisco, the Tracy Police Department said Saturday.
According to the school, Pribble is the varsity football head coach and a physical education teacher.
Pribble has held the coaching position for five years and has 22 years of experience as an educator with the district, according to his Facebook page.
SCHOOL EMPLOYEE ACCUSED OF SECRETLY FILMING 12 GIRLS IN CHANGING ROOM FACES NEW CHARGES
Jeffrey Pribble, the PE teacher and football coach at Tracy High School in California, will remain on leave while authorities continue investigating.  (Jeffrey Pribble/Facebook)
The discovery was made Thursday when a student and several classmates found the phone recording inside the locker room, officials said.
The students stopped the recording, deleted the video and turned the device over to a teacher.
By Thursday evening, a concerned parent then contacted Tracy police patrol officers, prompting school resource officers and detectives to open an investigation.
The following day, officers determined that the phone belonged to Pribble, who was arrested Friday.
The Tracy Unified School District placed Pribble on leave pending the outcome of separate criminal and district investigations, officials said.
In a statement to Fox News Digital on Monday, the district clarified that Pribble was placed on leave before his arrest on campus grounds.
"We are deeply concerned about the allegations and remain focused on protecting the safety of our students," the school added.
"The District is fully cooperating with law enforcement and we are not able to provide specific details about the allegations, as this is an ongoing investigation."
FLORIDA MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER ADMITS TO YEARS OF 'INAPPROPRIATE' CONVERSATIONS WITH FORMER STUDENT: DEPUTIES
FILE — People walk into Tracy High School in Tracy, California, where football coach Jeffrey Pribble was arrested Friday. (Google Maps)
According to the Pleasanton Weekly, Tracy High Principal Jon Waggle also addressed the arrest in an email to parents.

"We understand that this news may raise serious concerns in the District community. The District too is concerned about the well-being of its students and staff and is committed to holding its employees to the highest professional and ethical standards," Waggle wrote.

"Tracy High School and all our Tracy Unified schools are proud of being safe schools. The cooperation between students, parents and staff members keeps our schools safe and is important and appreciated. Thank you for your continued partnership and support."
Tracy Police Chief Sekou Millington added that the safety and privacy of the city's students remain among the department's top priorities.
"Our children deserve to feel safe at school and in every space where they should be able to learn, grow, and simply be kids," Millington said.
FILE — Jeffrey Pribble served as Tracy High School’s varsity football coach for five years and worked in the district for 22 years, according to his Facebook page. (Google Maps)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Protecting the safety, privacy, and well-being of our students is a responsibility we take seriously. We are grateful to the students who brought this incident to the attention of adults and to the officers and detectives who acted quickly to investigate."
Fox News Digital reached out to Tracy High School for more information.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Maryland dad blamed 'Satan' after 2-month-old daughter died from horrific head trauma
summary: A Maryland father blamed "Satan" for his 2-month-old daughter's fatal head trauma that led to her death, as he and the child's mother are facing child abuse charges.
story: Meliza Campos-Sanchez is facing two counts of child neglect, one count of child abuse and an arson charge stemming from an Aug. 16 incident, authorities said. (WSVN)

A Maryland couple was arrested after the death of their 2-month-old daughter who suffered head injuries, with the father allegedly telling police the girl's injuries were caused by "Satan slamming a door on the child," according to charging documents and prosecutors.

Oscar Pineda and Katerin Monzon-Alvarado, both 21, are facing charges for first- and second-degree child abuse, first- and second-degree assault and reckless endangerment that carry a maximum possible sentence of 55 years in prison in connection with the death of 2-month-old Aida Mikea Monzon Alvarado, Baltimore Police said, adding that they could face additional homicide charges pending the outcome of the autopsy report.

The baby was taken to Harbor Hospital on Wednesday with what doctors described as "suspicious" severe bruising around her eyes and jawline. A later examination revealed what charging documents describe as "significant head and brain trauma" and "multiple skull fractures" that were not noticed during the initial examination, charging documents state, according to CBS Baltimore.
IDAHO MOM WHO CLAIMED VACCINES KILLED HER TWIN BABIES CHARGED WITH MURDERING HER KIDS
Oscar Pineda and Katerin Monzon-Alvarado, both 21, are facing charges for first- and second-degree child abuse, first- and second-degree assault and reckless endangerment. (Baltimore Police)

The girl's father allegedly claimed to police that his daughter was injured "due to a supernatural force or Satan slamming a door on the child." The mother said her 2-year-old son often jumps on the bed, which caused the baby to fall onto the floor, a prosecutor said at a court hearing on Friday, according to the outlet.
The prosecutor argued that the extent of the girl's injuries could not have been caused by a single fall from the bed.

Police said the girl's mother brought the baby to the hospital on Wednesday after she became unresponsive. The woman initially told police the baby became unresponsive while lying face down in their bed after she was fed.
ALABAMA MOM CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER TODDLER BOUND, LEFT TO SUFFOCATE FOR 12 HOURS: COPS
The baby was taken to Harbor Hospital with what doctors described as "suspicious" severe bruising around her eyes and jawline. (Baltimore Police)
Prosecutors said the mother told investigators the child was "freezing and in shock" when she took her to the hospital.
Doctors said the baby "suffered from significant head and brain trauma" and "sustained frontal lobe hemorrhaging and a subdural hemorrhage," according to the charging documents.
Hospital staff could not revive the child, and she died in the hospital.
The girl's father allegedly told police that his daughter was injured "due to a supernatural force or Satan slamming a door on the child." (Tribune News Service via Getty)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Both parents later admitted to investigators that they noticed the girl's bruises on Sept. 6 and that she began vomiting the following day. They said they did not seek medical treatment until she was unresponsive on Wednesday.
The pair is Guatemalan nationals, and prosecutors argued they pose "an extreme flight risk."
Both parents were held without bail.

title: Creepy 'Cat in the Hat' trend targets schools as costumed figure allegedly chases teen girl
summary: A person dressed as the Cat in the Hat allegedly chased a teen girl in British Columbia as the creepy trend sparks school threats nationwide.
story: Citrus County Sheriff David Vincent warns families about disturbing social media posts targeting students, schools and communities. Credit: Citrus County Sheriff's Office

A shadowy figure dressed as the Cat in the Hat allegedly chased a teenage girl through a Canadian neighborhood, as a creepy online trend featuring sinister depictions of the beloved children’s character has prompted investigations and school warnings targeting schools and students across multiple states.

The unidentified girl was walking in West Kelowna, British Columbia, at about 9 p.m. Aug. 24 when a person wearing a costume resembling the Dr. Seuss character allegedly began chasing her, according to the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.
The teen escaped and reached her home safely, but police are still working to identify the costumed individual.
POLICE IDENTIFY SUSPECT ACCUSED OF TERRORIZING PHILADELPHIA WOMEN WHILE WEARING CREEPY CHUCKY-STYLE MASK
A grainy nighttime image shows an unidentified person wearing a Cat in the Hat-style costume as authorities investigate the disturbing trend. (West Kelowna RCMP)
"Regardless of whether the individual intended the behavior as a joke, following a young person and causing them to fear for their safety is extremely concerning," Cpl. Devon Gerrits said.
"People should understand that behavior intended as a prank can have serious consequences when it causes another person to reasonably fear for their safety."
TIMELINE REVEALS HOW MAN IN 'CHUCKY' MASK TERRORIZED PHILADELPHIA STREETS, EVADED POLICE
A phone displays a viral social media video showing a costumed Cat in the Hat figure standing outside a Publix store at night. (Citrus County Sheriff's Office)

Investigators said wearing a costume is not a crime by itself, but pursuing someone in a way that causes reasonable fear could constitute criminal harassment. Assault, threats or intimidation charges could also be considered depending on the evidence.
Anyone who believes they are being followed or pursued should move toward a populated location, contact a trusted adult and call 911 if they are in immediate danger, the West Kelowna RCMP advised.
Police are asking anyone with doorbell, security or dashcam video taken near the 2000 block of Shamrock Drive at about 9 p.m. Aug. 24 to contact the West Kelowna RCMP.

Police have not said whether the real-world chase is connected to a separate "Cat in the Hat" social media trend that has spread across the United States, putting schools on alert and landing some juveniles in custody.
LOUDOUN COUNTY TRANSGENDER SUBSTITUTE CHARGED WITH MAKING SCHOOL THREATS
An edited image places a Cat in the Hat figure outside a small-town theater alongside a message suggesting an extended "visit." (Citrus County Sheriff's Office)

The online trend features edited or AI-generated images and videos depicting a sinister version of the Cat in the Hat lurking outside homes, standing near schools or prowling through communities. Some anonymous accounts have added the names of students, staff members, campuses and towns, sometimes accompanied by ominous messages or threats.
Authorities from California to Florida, Virginia and Texas have responded with investigations and increased patrols as they work to separate internet hoaxes from credible dangers.
TIKTOK IN LEGAL HOT SEAT AS STATE ACCUSES APP OF EXPOSING KIDS TO HARMFUL CONTENT WHILE MISLEADING PARENTS
The Baldwin Park Police Department in California said it was reviewing "concerning social media posts" that referenced local schools and named students and staff members.
"Any threat directed toward our schools, students, staff, or community will not be dismissed as a joke or prank," the department warned.
NEW MEXICO SEEKS MASSIVE PENALTY FROM META AFTER JURY FOUND TECH GIANT LIABLE FOR ENDANGERING CHILDREN
Social media posts show a person in a Cat in the Hat costume referencing George West, Texas. (Citrus County Sheriff's Office)

Police urged residents not to interact with or recirculate the accounts. Anyone who encounters a threatening post is asked to preserve the content, account name, screenshots, dates and times before reporting it to investigators.

In Virginia, the Hanover County Sheriff’s Office launched an investigation after an account posted content referencing Mechanicsville High School and the trend. Deputies increased their presence at the campus while attempting to identify the person behind the account.
UK TO BAN TIKTOK, YOUTUBE, OTHER SOCIAL MEDIA APPS FOR CHILDREN UNDER 16, STARMER SAYS
A social media post shows a Cat in the Hat figure with an ominous message referencing Northampton and the Rushden and Higham area. (Citrus County Sheriff's Office)
The sheriff’s office similarly urged residents not to repost the material, warning that doing so could amplify the message and complicate efforts to trace its origin.

Florida’s St. Johns County Sheriff’s Office said it was investigating content involving county schools but had not identified a credible threat. Deputies nevertheless increased their presence on campuses across the county as a precaution.
Texas law enforcement agencies have also warned that creating or spreading the threatening posts could carry consequences far beyond school discipline.
The Frio County Sheriff’s Office said some anonymous accounts have attached lists of students, schools or communities to menacing images and videos in an apparent attempt to provoke fear.
Authorities there determined posts mentioning the area did not appear to present a credible threat but increased patrols and law enforcement visibility around schools.

"Participating in, re-creating, or spreading these threatening posts is not a harmless joke," the sheriff’s office said, warning that copycat accounts and forwarded threats could lead to charges involving cyberbullying, harassment or terroristic threats.
Laredo police delivered a similar warning, saying criminal charges and arrests may follow even when the person responsible claims the post was only meant as a prank.
GIRL OBSESSED WITH SANDY HOOK, COLUMBINE ALLEGEDLY PLOTTED SCHOOL MASSACRE WITH OTHER STUDENTS: REPORT
A disturbing social media post shows a Cat in the Hat figure beneath a local water tower with the message, "look familiar?" (Citrus County Sheriff's Office)
"A few seconds on social media can result in a police investigation, school disciplinary action, and potentially serious criminal consequences," the department said.

Premont police met with school district leaders after learning of the trend and warned that fake accounts, AI-generated content and purported pranks involving threats could result in charges including making a terroristic threat or filing a false alarm or report under Texas law.
The warnings come as authorities in multiple states have traced threatening accounts to juveniles.

Four girls between 13 and 15 years old were arrested in Berwick, Louisiana, after police linked them to TikTok accounts that alarmed families and schools, according to Police1. Three were charged with terrorizing or menacing, while a fourth was charged with cyberbullying.

A 12-year-old Florida student was accused of posting a written threat to kill tied to the trend, while a 14-year-old Colorado student was arrested after a post referenced a middle school and several homes, the outlet reported. Authorities in Alabama, Ohio and Kentucky have also announced juvenile arrests or pending charges connected to similar posts.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Police across the affected communities have repeatedly asked parents and students not to share the content, even when attempting to warn others. Instead, users should capture screenshots showing the account name and threatening material and send the evidence directly to school officials or law enforcement.
Fox News Digital reached out to TikTok for comment.

title: Missing 70-year-old hiker rescued after disappearing for a week in remote national park
summary: A Coast Guard helicopter crew hoisted Craig Berg to safety after he went missing for a week while hiking in Michigan’s remote Isle Royale National Park.
story: Craig Berg, 70, was found injured and suffering from hypothermia after disappearing during an extended solo hike. (U.S. Coast Guard Great Lakes)
A 70-year-old man who vanished a week ago while hiking in Isle Royale National Park was found "alive and alert" Saturday, according to officials.
Craig Berg was suffering from hypothermia when he was rescued by Coast Guard and Michigan State Police crews, officials said.
"The Coast Guard and Michigan State Police rescued an injured, ailing man Saturday after he went missing in Isle Royale National Park on Sept. 5," the U.S. Coast Guard Great Lakes said.

Video released by authorities shows a helicopter crew from Coast Guard Air Station Traverse City hoisting Berg from the ground. He was then taken to a regional airport in Gwinn for emergency medical evaluation.
MISSOURI DEPUTY AG, MISSING 6 DAYS AFTER SEEKING TO SUMMIT WYOMING'S TALLEST PEAK, IS FOUND ALIVE
A Coast Guard helicopter crew hoists Craig Berg, 70, from Isle Royale National Park in Lake Superior on Sept. 12, 2026. (USCGGreatLakes; Berg Family via Isle Royale National Park)
Officials did not disclose what happened to Berg while he was missing or provide additional details about his injuries.
Berg was spotted by "good Samaritan" backpackers in the park Saturday before Michigan State Police foot patrols and K-9 units reached him, according to officials.
Multiple agencies and resources were deployed to aid the emergency search, which also included a 45-foot Coast Guard boat, drones and seaplanes.

The search involved the National Park Service, Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Keweenaw County Sheriff’s Office, Wisconsin State Patrol and Minnesota Department of Public Safety, according to Lt. Ben Eckola, a Michigan State Police public information officer.

"We’re also thankful to the fellow hikers who helped, Isle Royale Seaplanes, and No One Left Behind K9 Search and Rescue. Everyone’s efforts played an important part in finding Craig," Eckola said in a statement.
ILLINOIS MAN MISSING MORE THAN A WEEK AS CREWS SCOUR GREAT SMOKY MOUNTAINS NATIONAL PARK
Michigan State Police K-9 officers sit aboard a Coast Guard helicopter over Lake Superior en route to Isle Royale National Park on Sept. 11, 2026. (USCGGreatLakes, courtesy Air Station Traverse City)
The Detroit Free Press reported that Berg, of Royal Oak, Michigan, arrived at the national park on Aug. 27 for an extended solo hike but failed to return home Sept. 5.
Isle Royale National Park is located on a remote island in Lake Superior near the Canadian border.
Due to its remote location, Isle Royale is one of the least-visited national parks and has limited infrastructure.
Berg’s wife, Debbie, told the Detroit Free Press that only two rangers are stationed on the island and that the park has two camp stores and a lodge.
Officials deployed water, land and air crews to search for Craig Berg after he went missing on Sept. 5, 2026. (USCGGreatLakes)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
According to the park’s website, cell phone service is often "unreliable," and many types of equipment are generally prohibited on the island, including bicycles, motorized vehicles and drones.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Accused killers vanish after family massacre before manhunt ends hundreds of miles away
summary: A deadly North Carolina shooting left two dead and two critically injured before suspects Camryn Moore and Cory Armstrong fled across state lines.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A deadly shooting inside a North Carolina family home triggered an urgent search for two accused killers and an interstate manhunt that would end with another burst of gunfire.
Gaston County Police officers responded to a home on Forbes Road at approximately 8:43 a.m. Thursday after receiving a report of gunfire inside the residence.
Officers discovered four people suffering from gunshot wounds. Two were pronounced dead at the scene, while two others were rushed to CaroMont Regional Medical Center with life-threatening injuries.

Police identified the two people killed as Victoria "Heather" Moore, 50, and Megan "Josiah" Bumgardner, 38. The two surviving victims remained in critical but stable condition Friday, according to police.
4 SHOT INSIDE NORTH CAROLINA HOME, 2 KILLED AS POLICE IDENTIFY PERSON OF INTEREST
Gaston County police responded to the Forbes Road home after receiving a report of gunfire inside. (Queen City News)

Detectives identified two residents of the home, Camryn Moore, 26, and Cory Armstrong, 29, as suspects in the bloodshed. WSOC-TV reported that Heather Moore was Camryn Moore’s mother and Bumgardner was her uncle.
Cory Armstrong, 29, was wanted on murder and attempted murder charges following a shooting at a Gaston County home. (Gaston County Police)
Police said they believed everyone involved knew one another and described the shooting as an isolated incident with no continuing threat to the Gaston County community.
Camryn Moore, 26, was accused of killing two people and critically wounding two others inside a North Carolina home. (Gaston County Police)
Investigators have not disclosed what may have triggered the violence.

Camryn Moore and Armstrong allegedly fled Gaston County immediately after the shooting. By Thursday afternoon, detectives had obtained warrants charging each of them with two counts of first-degree murder and two counts of attempted first-degree murder.
WATCH: DEPUTIES HUNT WANTED MAN THROUGH CORNFIELD AFTER HIGH-SPEED CHASE CAUGHT ON CAMERA
Gaston County Police identified two suspects after four people were found shot inside a family home. (Queen City News)

The Gaston County Police Department enlisted the help of the U.S. Marshals Service Carolinas Regional Fugitive Task Force as investigators tracked the pair’s movements across multiple states overnight.
SUSPECTED HUMAN SMUGGLERS LEAD COPS ON 100-MPH CHASE BEFORE BAILING AND ALLEGEDLY COMMITTING ARMED CARJACKING
The search reached Ohio at approximately 8 a.m. Friday, when state troopers spotted the suspects’ vehicle outside Athens and attempted to pull it over, authorities said.
Moore and Armstrong allegedly refused to stop, setting off a multi-county pursuit.

The chase came to a violent end when their vehicle swerved to avoid spike strips deployed in the roadway and crashed, according to information provided to North Carolina investigators by Ohio authorities.
A street view shows the Forbes Road address identified by police in connection with the deadly Gaston County shooting. (Google Maps)
Officers then reported hearing two gunshots coming from the wrecked vehicle.
Law enforcement deployed a drone to look inside and discovered Moore and Armstrong dead. Authorities have not disclosed who fired the shots or officially announced the manner of their deaths.
The Ohio State Highway Patrol is investigating the pursuit, crash and deaths.
Back in Gastonia, neighbors were stunned by the violence that shattered their normally peaceful street.
Loretta Forbes, whose husband’s grandfather built her home in 1914 and gave Forbes Road its name, told WSOC-TV that she knew the family living next door.
"I just kept saying, ‘My God. Oh God,’ coming down the stairs," Forbes told the outlet. "They seem to be very nice people. It just shakes you up to think that could happen so close by."
Forbes said she was praying for the family and searching for answers.
"I want to know what’s happened," she said. "I want to know about the family."
Jennifer Greene, a friend and co-worker of Heather Moore, drove to the home after Moore unexpectedly failed to report for her shift.
SUSPECTED DUI DRIVER LEADS COPS ON WILD CHASE BEFORE DRAMATIC TAKEDOWN ON POPULAR CALIFORNIA BEACH
Friends remembered Victoria "Heather" Moore as a warm and loving person after she was killed in the Gaston County shooting. (Heather Moore Facebook)
"This was a tragic act of violence that resulted in the loss of multiple lives and left others critically injured," the Gaston County Police Department said.
"Although the search for the suspects has ended, our investigation has not," police added.
Heather Moore, left, was remembered by friends as a loving woman who brought warmth into every room. (GoFundMe)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Anyone with information about the shooting is asked to contact Detective G. Lancaster at 704-866-3320 or CrimeStoppers at 704-861-8000.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Gaston County Police Department and Ohio State Highway Patrol for additional information.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Charlie Kirk statue defaced with red paint, Jesus crossed out days after 1-year mark of assassination
summary: Red paint was smeared across the Charlie Kirk statue at Turning Point USA's Phoenix headquarters, with a Christian tribute defaced days after unveiling.
story: President Donald Trump honors Charlie Kirk during a speech at the RNC midterm convention. 'The Five' co-hosts reflect on Kirk's legacy, his impact through Turning Point USA, and the expansion of the group to more than 3,500 high school clubs one year after his assassination.

Vandals smeared bright red paint across a newly unveiled statue of Charlie Kirk and defaced a Christian tribute outside Turning Point USA’s Phoenix headquarters early Sunday, just three days after the memorial was installed.
Images from the headquarters show red paint streaked across the eight-foot statue’s face and neck, with a crude frowning face drawn across its chest.

A sign at the base of the statue bearing Kirk’s image and the words "Jesus defeated death so you can live" was also targeted. The word "Jesus" and an image of a cross appeared to be crossed out, while "Satan" was apparently scrawled across the display.
REMEMBERING CHARLIE KIRK: TURNING POINT USA'S ANDREW KOLVET REFLECTS ON CONSERVATIVE GROUP'S CHALLENGING YEAR
Kirk's widow, Erika, who now serves as Turning Point USA CEO, responded with a defiant vow to rebuild, saying the vandals would not erase her husband’s legacy or silence Christians.
"Charlie once said we should be building two statues for every statue that they tear down," Erika Kirk wrote, adding that her husband’s instinct was always to create rather than destroy.

She said the bullet that killed her husband only amplified his voice and predicted the spray paint would spread his legacy even further. She also vowed to restore the statue, replace Jesus Christ’s name on the damaged sign and continue the movement her husband built.
"God will not be mocked," Erika Kirk wrote.
Phoenix police confirmed to Fox News Digital that the department began receiving calls around 8:09 a.m. reporting vandalism to a memorial in the area of 4900 East Beverly Road.
"Officers have responded to the location, and the incident is under investigation," police said.
No arrests or suspect descriptions had been announced as of Sunday afternoon.

"This morning we woke up to radical criminals vandalizing our headquarters," Turning Point USA Chief Operating Officer Tyler Bowyer wrote on social media. "Crossing over Charlie’s face, scratching out Jesus and the Cross and spraying red paint on his neck.
"This isn’t the country we want to live in," Bowyer added. "Arizona is not Gotham."
INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES
Bowyer, who went to the headquarters as police investigated, said TPUSA was prepared to clean the memorial as soon as authorities released the scene.
"God bless the police as they investigate the violent thugs who did this," Bowyer wrote.
TPUSA also released video showing the damage and encouraged its supporters to vote ahead of the midterm elections.
"Hate cannot win," the organization wrote. "The radical Left is showing up to vote. What are you doing to save the country from this?"
In a follow-up statement, TPUSA said it would restore the statue and replace the damaged signs while reviewing footage of the incident and working with law enforcement to identify those responsible.
"Vandalism like this is not funny, it’s diabolical," the organization wrote. "The incident happened in the middle of the night because evil never sleeps."
TPUSA said the vandals went beyond spraying Kirk’s face and neck with red paint, accusing them of making an "intentional decision" to cross out Jesus’ name on the nearby sign.
The organization ended its response by quoting John 15:18: "If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first."
Later Sunday, TPUSA spokesman Andrew Kolvet announced that the statue had been restored.
"The team rallied and got the statue back looking good as new," Kolvet wrote. "Evil may never sleep, but neither do we."
"We won’t stop. We will win. They will lose," he added.
The vandalism struck only days after TPUSA unveiled the bronze statue Thursday to mark one year since Kirk was assassinated while speaking at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025.
CHARLIE KIRK STATUE BOUND FOR NY'S TIMES SQUARE AS SCULPTOR DEFIES THREATS AHEAD OF UNVEILING
A person visits the makeshift memorial for Charlie Kirk outside the headquarters of Turning Point USA on September 18, 2025, in Phoenix, Arizona. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)
The statue depicts Kirk wearing his signature "Freedom" T-shirt and cross necklace. Those who knew him said the sculpture captured details down to his wedding ring, according to FOX 10 Phoenix.

Turning Point USA commissioned Utah artist Quintin McCann to create the memorial after he began working on a portrait of Kirk the evening the conservative activist was killed, according to the outlet.
ITALIAN ARTIST UNVEILS CHARLIE KIRK MEMORIAL STATUE HE PLANS TO FEATURE AT TIMES SQUARE

"Someone’s death, who I’ve never met, has never impacted me so much," McCann told FOX 10. "And I’m sure many people can agree. And I just stayed at work that evening and just started sculpting his portrait."
The statue was initially placed outside TPUSA’s headquarters near 48th Street and Beverly Road but was expected to be moved indoors for security reasons by the end of the week, the outlet reported.
REPUBLICAN CONVENTION ATTENDEES SHARE HEARTFELT TRIBUTES TO LATE CHARLIE KIRK ON ASSASSINATION ANNIVERSARY
Conservative voices erupted over the attack, condemning the vandalism as another assault on Kirk’s family, friends and legacy.
"Truly abhorrent," Rep. Abe Hamadeh, R-Ariz., wrote on X. "The Charlie Kirk statue that was just unveiled at Turning Point’s HQ was vandalized overnight with red paint.

"The young people who work at Turning Point don’t deserve this, Charlie’s family doesn’t deserve this, his friends don’t deserve this," Hamadeh added. "The left is intolerant and militant. Evil exists and must be confronted continuously."
Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., was equally blunt.
"This is absolute evil," Biggs wrote.
Conservative commentator Benny Johnson accused the vandals of trying to intimidate Kirk’s supporters.
"These people are incapable of building anything, all they know is destruction," Johnson wrote. "Keep these demons out of power."
TPUSA contributor Alex Clark said seeing the damage brought her to tears before issuing a dire warning to conservative voters.
"The left wants to tap dance in your blood and throw confetti at your gravestone," Clark wrote. "Vote red in midterms like your life depends on it because it actually does as a conservative."

Turning Point USA Chief of Staff Mikey McCoy urged conservatives to answer the vandalism with faith, invoking Kirk’s willingness to return to hostile campuses and the biblical examples of Stephen and Christ praying for those who persecuted them.

"Then I can surrender all the anger, and pure disgust that I feel at seeing this to a just and holy God," McCoy wrote, saying he would pray instead for the repentance and salvation of those responsible.
"Lord, help our Country," he added. "Open their eyes. Break their hearts. Save them."

Bowyer also blasted Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs, accusing her of failing to pursue bipartisanship after Kirk’s killing and pointing to her veto of legislation that would have named Loop 202 in Kirk’s honor.

Hobbs said in her March veto letter that she condemned political violence but argued highway-naming decisions should remain nonpartisan and be handled by the state board responsible for such designations.

Charlie Kirk speaks at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025 in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking on his American Comeback Tour when he was shot and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)
Kirk was 31 when he was shot and killed during a TPUSA event at Utah Valley University.
Tyler Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges in Kirk’s death. Prosecutors are seeking the death penalty.

Erika Kirk took over as CEO of Turning Point USA after her husband’s assassination. The conservative organization he co-founded in 2012 has continued expanding its network of high school and college chapters since his death.

Anyone with information about the vandalism is asked to contact Phoenix police or Silent Witness at 480-WITNESS.
Fox News Digital has reached out to Turning Point USA and Hobbs’ office for additional information and comment.

title: Arrest rips apart media narrative on death of Black woman found hanging from Mississippi tree
summary: Jarques Ratliff faces a murder charge in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old mother found hanging from a tree behind a Jackson, Mississippi home.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Mississippi authorities have arrested a 51-year-old man on a murder charge after an official homicide ruling in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old Black mother of four found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned home last month.

The arrest follows weeks of intense media attention and widespread online discussion regarding the circumstances surrounding Fortune’s death in a state with a historic legacy of racialized violence. But law enforcement officials confirmed that the suspect taken into custody is Jarques Ratliff, a Black Jackson resident who had a prior personal connection with Fortune.

Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney announced during a news conference Saturday that Ratliff was taken into custody without incident while walking along Capitol Street in Jackson, shortly after officers executed search warrants at related properties.
AOC’S ‘MODERN-DAY LYNCHINGS’ CLAIM TORN TO SHREDS ONLINE AS BLACK HANGING CASE FINDINGS TELL A DIFFERENT STORY

Chief Brackney emphasized that while the arrest marks a significant breakthrough, the investigation remains active and additional arrest warrants are expected to be served as detectives follow further leads.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., last week warned of "racial terror" and "widespread modern-day lynchings" in the U.S. as she joined dozens of Democrats demanding that the Department of Justice investigate hanging deaths of Black Americans.
Christy Spivey poses with a portrait of her late daughter Tasia Fortune Sept. 8, 2026, in Marion, Ky. (AP Photo/George Walker IV)
Fortune’s body was discovered Aug. 3 in the backyard of a vacant property in the 500 block of Road of Remembrance in Jackson.

Although investigators logged hundreds of hours interviewing nearly 15 individuals and reviewing physical evidence over the past month, formal arrest warrants could not be executed until the Mississippi State Medical Examiner’s Office officially classified Fortune’s death a homicide late Thursday.

Once that classification was handed down, members of the Jackson Police Department's robbery-homicide unit moved swiftly to secure and execute two search warrants alongside the arrest warrant for Ratliff.

Addressing public interest in the case, Chief Brackney acknowledged the heightened scrutiny but stressed that law enforcement remains strictly guided by verifiable physical evidence rather than external speculation. She noted that authorities understood public concern given Mississippi's history but said the department is bound to ensure all public statements are backed by forensic facts.
Tasia Fortune in a portrait displayed Sept. 8, 2026, in Marion, Ky. Inset: Jarques Ratliff, who was arrested in connection to Fortune's death. (AP Photo/George Walker IV; Jackson Police Department)

"We understand that this case has received media attention from across the globe and across the community. We understand the questions and the desire for answers given Mississippi's history," Brackney said.

"We understand this case is being viewed through a broader lens — a global lens — and we do not dismiss those concerns. We are taking them seriously. At the same time, we do have a responsibility to make sure that what we say publicly is supported by our evidence and the facts."

Brackney also directly clarified that law enforcement had never officially designated any persons of interest prior to Ratliff’s arrest, refuting social media reports that a 65-year-old man had previously been identified as a suspect.
Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney speaking at a news conference. (Jackson Police Department)
COPS DROP MURDER PROBE AFTER CORONER RULES MAN’S BLOODY STABBING DEATH WAS FREAK ACCIDENT

Fortune's mother, Christy Spivey, said police promptly notified her family of the homicide ruling and Ratliff's arrest on Friday. Spivey expressed gratitude for the police work and reiterated her firm belief that her daughter did not die by suicide, adding that Fortune would never take her own life.
Police say Fortune’s body was discovered Aug. 3 in the backyard of a vacant property in the 500 block of Road of Remembrance in Jackson. (Google Maps)

According to family members and an online obituary published in Kentucky, Fortune grew up in Kentucky, skipped her junior year of high school and was a star cross-country runner guided by strong religious faith before relocating to Jackson a decade ago.
Spivey noted that her daughter had experienced homelessness in recent years but was actively working to launch a cleaning business and stabilize her life prior to her death.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Ratliff is being held at the Hinds County Detention Center on a charge of murder. According to Mississippi State Defender André de Gruy, Ratliff is scheduled to make his initial appearance in Jackson Municipal Court no later than Monday morning, where formal charges will be read and bond conditions set.

Police have not publicly detailed the specific physical evidence linking Ratliff to the scene, nor have they expanded on the exact nature of his personal association with Fortune as investigators prepare for further potential arrests.
Bradford Betz is a Fox News Digital breaking reporter covering crime, political issues, and much more.

title: Female passenger undresses on American Airlines flight, engages in 'indecent acts,' crew reports
summary: A female passenger on American Airlines Flight 1779 reportedly undressed and performed indecent acts mid-flight, prompting law enforcement at Miami.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Law enforcement officers met an American Airlines flight upon its arrival at Miami International Airport late Friday night following reports of a female passenger undressing and behaving indecently mid-flight.

American Airlines Flight 1779 departed Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI) just after 9 p.m. EDT on Friday, Sept. 11, 2025, nearly two hours behind its scheduled departure time, according to public flight-tracking data. The flight landed in Miami at approximately 11:23 p.m. EDT.
As the Airbus A319 was en route to Florida, flight attendants alerted the cockpit crew to a disturbance involving a passenger in row 9.
UNRULY PASSENGERS COULD BE BANNED FOR LIFE FROM MULTIPLE AIRLINES UNDER NEW PROPOSAL
An American Airlines jet at Miami International Airport averting a near tragedy Friday night. (Ronen Tivony/NurPhoto)

According to Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS) datalink logs published by aviation website AirLive, the lead flight attendant reported that a female passenger in seat 9D had completely undressed and engaged in indecent acts in view of nearby passengers.
An American Airlines flight after landing at Chicago O'Hare International Airport on Aug. 17. (Marcin Golba/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
The ACARS message stated the incident was required to be reported to American Airlines’ Integrated Operations Center and that law enforcement should be requested.
FRONTIER PASSENGERS TACKLE MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY CHOKED OFF-DUTY FLIGHT ATTENDANT, TRIED TO OPEN DOOR MID-FLIGHT

The flight continued to Miami without diverting and arrived at Gate D2 in Terminal N, according to flight tracking service Flightera. AirLive reported that law enforcement officers were waiting at the gate and that the passenger was taken into custody.
An American Airlines Boeing 737-800 sits at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport in Dallas, Texas, on Nov. 23, 2017. (Getty Images)
It remains unclear what specific measures cabin crew took during the flight to manage the disturbance.

title: Iran's regime came for teenage twins. Their fate offers a glimpse of Tehran's widening death campaign
summary: Iranian twins Taraneh and Romina Rahimi face execution and decades in prison after joining protests, as Iran's death penalty surge draws global alarm.
story: Behnam Ben Taleblu says Tehran is using executions, arrests and internet shutdowns to suppress dissent and deter another nationwide uprising.
Taraneh and Romina Rahimi were 19, still in high school and living with their mother when masked men came for them in the middle of the night.

According to their U.S.-based cousin, the twin sisters were dragged from their beds with bags placed over their heads about a month after they joined anti-regime protests in Isfahan. Their family was given no explanation and spent months searching courts, hospitals and government offices trying to determine where they had been taken.
Four months later, their mother, Marzieh Nourmohammadi, was finally allowed to see them at Dowlatabad Prison. She barely recognized her daughters.
ONE GLARING ISSUE GOES UNADDRESSED IN UN CHIEF'S HIGH-STAKES TALKS WITH IRAN'S PRESIDENT
Iranian twins Taraneh and Romina Rahimi were arrested after joining anti-regime protests in Isfahan, Iran. Taraneh has been sentenced to death, while Romina faces decades in prison. (HANA)

Their cousin, Masoud Nourmohammadi, told The Guardian that the twins had badly swollen and bruised faces, injuries to their elbows, hands and feet, and significant hair loss that he said resulted from guards pulling them by their hair as they were moved between cells. He said their mother also learned that the sisters had been held in solitary confinement.

Now 20, Taraneh Rahimi faces execution over her alleged role in the January protests, while her twin sister could spend decades in prison, in a case unfolding amid a sharp rise in Iran’s use of the death penalty.

Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) reported that Taraneh was sentenced to death and an additional 11 years in prison, while Romina received a 36-year sentence. The sentences were issued by Branch 1 of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court and remain initial-stage verdicts.

The twins are among 16 defendants prosecuted in what has become known as the "Isfahan Shohada Square" case. HRANA said 10 defendants received death sentences and the 16 defendants collectively received 256 years in prison.
The sisters’ family says the abuse was intended to force confessions.
IRAN JAILS PSYCHOLOGIST OVER TRUMP PLEA AS REGIME DEMANDS HE MAKE AMERICANS ‘LOOK STUPID’: FAMILY
Taraneh Rahimi, 20, has been sentenced to death over her alleged role in anti-regime protests in Isfahan, Iran. Her family says she was tortured in custody and forced to confess. (HANA)

Nourmohammadi told The Guardian that Taraneh was threatened that prison guards would rape Romina in front of her unless she signed a confession. The outlet reported that Taraneh later told the court that admissions attributed to her had been obtained through torture. Her mother was not permitted to attend the trial, according to the family.

Radio Farda separately reported, citing Nourmohammadi, that the sisters suffered physical and psychological abuse and were forced to confess to accusations they deny. The Hana Human Rights Organization told Fox News Digital they have verified the torture allegations.

Concerns about torture extend beyond the sisters. HRANA reported that another defendant in the same case, Ahmadreza Saeidi, told judges during the hearing that the investigating judge personally used an electric stun gun on his neck and genitals. Defense lawyers also reportedly complained that they had not been given access to substantial portions of the case file or adequate time to examine evidence before trial.
The sentences come as rights organizations document a sharp rise in executions across Iran.
COULD NARGES MOHAMMADI UNITE IRAN’S OPPOSITION? HUSBAND SAYS IMPRISONED NOBEL LAUREATE STILL FIGHTING

A picture of Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi on the wall of the Grand Hotel in central Oslo before the Nobel banquet, in connection with the awarding of the Nobel Peace Prize 2023, in Oslo, Norway, Dec. 10, 2023. (NTB/Javad Parsa via Reuters)

The Washington-based Abdorrahman Boroumand Center for Human Rights in Iran documented 901 executions during the first seven months of 2026, including 56 people executed on political or national-security charges.

Behnam Ben Taleblu, Iran program senior director at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital that the executions should be viewed as part of a broader campaign by Tehran to suppress dissent at home.

"Despite the war in the region, despite the drone war, the missile war, the war over the Strait of Hormuz, the real war is the one that's happening on a day-to-day basis inside the Islamic Republic," Ben Taleblu said. "The Islamic Republic is quite literally cracking skulls, cracking down on civil society, on dissidents, on protesters."
Among those imprisoned in Iran’s broader crackdown is Seyed Ahmad Seyedabdollahi, a 32-year-old psychologist whose case Fox News Digital reported in August.

Seyed Ahmad Seyedabdollahi, a 32-year-old Iranian psychologist, who addressed President Donald Trump in an English-language video posted on Jan. 4, 2026, urging him to follow through on his pledge to support Iranian protesters. Seyedabdollahi was arrested 10 days later and was subsequently sentenced to seven months in prison. (Fox News)

Seyedabdollahi posted an English-language video on Jan. 4 appealing directly to President Donald Trump to support Iranian protesters, according to his relatives and Fox News Digital’s previous reporting. He was arrested 10 days later and ultimately sentenced to seven months in prison and barred from government and public services for five years.

His relatives told Fox News Digital that Iranian authorities later pressured him to record another video insulting Trump and Americans and alleged that he was subjected to solitary confinement and torture.

The Hana Human Rights Organization reported Aug. 9 that Seyedabdollahi had been held in Borujen Prison since July 7 and that authorities opened a second case against him on a charge of "propaganda against the system of the Islamic Republic." Hana also confirmed that he was serving a seven-month sentence and had received a five-year disqualification from public and governmental services.

His relatives confirmed to Fox News Digital that authorities have continued pressuring him to say he was a "foreign agent" paid by the U.S. government. They also said authorities revoked his professional license, adding financial pressure on his family.
Ben Taleblu said Tehran has followed a similar pattern after previous periods of external conflict, turning its attention inward against perceived opponents.
INSIDE TEHRAN: IRANIANS DESCRIBE IRGC'S BRUTAL RULE, POVERTY — ASK TRUMP TO 'STAY THE COURSE'
Iranians attend an anti-government protest in Tehran, Iran, Jan. 9, 2026. (UGC via AP)
"We saw this trend in the aftermath of the 12-day war as well," Ben Taleblu said. "Lose a war abroad, come home and pretend like you're the victor."
"Simply here, the Islamic Republic is continuing the longest war it's ever fought, which is the 47-year war against the Iranian people," he added.

Wednesday marks four years since the Sept. 16, 2022, death of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish Iranian woman who was detained three days earlier by Iran’s morality police over what authorities described as "improper hijab." Her death sparked nationwide protests that became known internationally as the "Woman, Life, Freedom" movement. The U.N. said reports that Amini had been beaten in custody warranted an independent investigation, while Iranian authorities maintained that she died of "natural causes."
'KILLING OFF THE COUNTRY': IRAN EXECUTES DOZENS, ARRESTS 4,000-PLUS IN WAR CRACKDOWN
Protesters march in downtown Tehran, Iran, Monday, Dec. 29, 2025. (Fars News Agency via AP)

The 2022 uprising was itself part of a longer cycle of unrest. Nationwide demonstrations beginning in December 2017 rapidly spread across Iran and represented the largest challenge to the government since the 2009 Green Movement. The 2017-18 protests were followed by another major nationwide wave in 2019 and then the 2022 Woman, Life, Freedom uprising.

Ben Taleblu argued that whenever another major protest movement emerges, Western governments should be prepared to help Iranians communicate with one another and the outside world, particularly when authorities shut down internet access.

"We know every single time another major protest is happening, the way the regime cracks down is to first turn off the internet," he said. "That means the regime fears what comes of coordination between Iranians and fears what comes of when the Iranians are able to send their message outside to the international community."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Amirhossein Safari Hosseinabadi was hanged Tuesday in Isfahan's Shahid Alikhani Square — the same location where he had joined anti-government demonstrations months earlier. (HRANA)
"The partners of the Iranian people, America, Israel, the West, these are largely all cyber superpowers," Ben Taleblu said. "We should not let the Iranian people continue to die in the darkness."

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is a reporter for Fox News Digital with more than 15 years of experience covering conflict, global affairs, human rights and political accountability. She has directed and produced more than 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries, documenting conflicts, humanitarian crises, corruption, human trafficking, gender-based violence and the human stories behind major world events.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Europe’s left courts Muslim voters as anti-Israel politics reshape continent
summary: Europe’s far left is finding common ground with Islamist-linked networks on anti-Israel politics, creating a growing challenge for Jewish communities and voters.
story: A Muslim scholar who fled Egypt after criticizing Hamas warns that a growing alliance between radical left activists and Islamist groups could have serious consequences for Western democracies.

It's known as the "Red-Green Alliance" — a political coalition between Europe's far-left parties and Islamist groups that is increasingly shaping policy, particularly regarding Israel as the continent experiences a worrying rise in antisemitism that critics are linking to this partnership.
With the rise of Muslim voters across Europe, many on the left and extreme-left are being influenced by this increasingly important voting bloc.

Just last week in the U.K., critics accused the left-wing Labour government of sanctioning Israel as a ploy to win back Muslim voters from the far-left, anti-Israel Green and Independent parties. Conservative lawmaker Tom Tugendhat called the sanctions' announcement "performative politics."

In Sunday’s parliamentary elections in Sweden, exit polling from the state broadcaster shows that votes from non-European Swedes are giving an alliance of left-wing parties a narrow three-seat lead over a right-leaning coalition led by current Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson.
GERMAN OFFICIALS WARN ISLAMIST, FAR-LEFT RHETORIC DRIVING SPIKE IN ANTISEMITIC ATTACKS

Election campaign posters from the Social Democrats and Communist parties are displayed in a public area during Sweden's general elections in Stockholm, Sweden, on Sept. 13, 2026. (Atila Altuntas/Anadolu via Getty Images)

One Swedish political researcher, Tobias Hübinette, pointed to Mayor Zohran Mamdani's win in New York City and said that the numbers in the Swedish election show that this "election meant a 'Mamdanification' of urban Sweden, and the gap between city and country is now larger than ever before," he wrote on X.

"They should be in disagreement," Simone Rodan-Benzaquen, the senior envoy to Europe at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital, "but the Islamists are very capable of covering that up for political purposes… The antisemitism that we have today, in particular in Western Europe, is definitely fed far more (by) the far left's discourse."

Alan Mendoza, executive director of the Henry Jackson Society in the U.K. said that, "For a decade, Europe has trained its anxieties almost exclusively on the far-right, and while that vigilance is warranted, it has left a blind spot on the other flank… Antisemitism is not less dangerous because it arrives waving a progressive banner."

Germany-based Dresden University of Technology research fellow Janek Treiber said that, "There is indeed an intriguing alliance between the supposedly progressive left and regressive forces within Islamism." He told Fox News Digital that, "The unifying factor is a kind of victimization narrative. For the left that supports the Palestinian cause, Muslims are the oppressed and the West – including Israel – are the oppressors… Whether Muslims hold conservative-religious views in this context is irrelevant."
ANTI-MIGRANT AFD SEEKS TO BREAK GERMANY’S POLITICAL ‘FIREWALL’ IN HISTORIC STATE ELECTION
Protesters hold up flags and placards during a pro-Palestinian demonstration in London, Saturday, Jan. 13, 2024. (AP Photo/Alberto Pezzali)

Voters in Berlin head to the ballot box this coming Sunday, with polls showing the far-left Die Linke Party, literally translated as the "The Left," leading the center-right Christian Democratic Union by two points.

"In Berlin, a party polling at the top of the field has factions that share platforms, demonstrations and slogans with networks the German security services themselves link to Hamas and the PFLP," Mendoza claimed. "When 'Death to the IDF' and 'Intifada' are chanted at an election event, and the response from parts of the party is to defend the man who led them, the red line has been erased, not crossed."

Rodan-Benzaquen says that while Germany’s political "firewall" against far-right parties like the AfD "seems to work more or less on the right, it doesn't on the left," because, "there is a perception that whatever comes from the left, even the far-left, is not morally as repugnant as anything that comes from the right."
ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE REACHES DEADLIEST LEVEL SINCE 1994, NEW GLOBAL REPORT FINDS

Pro-Palestinian activists from the Ireland Palestine Solidarity Campaign, supported by members of left-wing parties including People Before Profit and the Socialist Party and students, participate in the National March for Palestine from the Garden of Remembrance to Connell Street and Leinster House, on May 18, 2024, in Dublin, Ireland. (Artur Widak/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Germany and the U.K. are not alone. The far-left Sumar Party in Spain is part of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s ruling coalition. Their support in the last election was strongest in areas with high Muslim populations, with party members attending demonstrations with Muslim Brotherhood-adjacent groups and Gaza protests organized by Islamist-leaning networks. Members have also pushed for Spain to recognize a Palestinian state while also referring to Israel as an "apartheid state." Spain recognized a Palestinian state in 2024.

The far-left La France Insoumise (LFI) Party in France has been accused by academics and ministers of "Islamo‑leftism" after their de facto leader, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, refused to call Hamas a terrorist organization and party members marched with Islamist-linked NGOs during Gaza protests. The LFI’s popularity has been on the rise in polling ahead of next year’s presidential election and, according to French newspaper Le Monde, the LFI’s electoral strength lies in Muslim-majority suburban districts.

Israeli Ambassador to France Joshua Zarka recently told Fox News Digital that, "The way [LFI leader] Jean-Luc Mélenchon speaks in front of a crowd reminds me of Hitler. The way he uses the idea of uniting against one enemy by speaking of Israel is similar to the way Hitler used to speak about the Jews."

Leader of French left-wing La France Insoumise (LFI) Party Jean-Luc Mélenchon delivers a speech during an electoral campaign meeting of the local LFI candidate for French municipal elections in Marseille, southern France, on March 7, 2026. (Miguel Medina / AFP via Getty Images)

Commenting on the sanctions imposed by the U.K. government on Israel, Britain's Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis called the announcement on X "a truly dark day for British Jews." His statement continued in part, "Gesture politics of this kind feeds into an increasingly hostile discourse about Israel," he wrote, warning that the cumulative effect of such policies could "further embolden those, at home and abroad, who use hatred as a weapon against Jews."
EXILED MUSLIM SCHOLAR WARNS FAR-LEFT–ISLAMIST ALLIANCE BEHIND ANTI-ISRAEL PROTESTS ECHOES IRAN’S RISE

Former Conservative Cabinet Minister Michael Gove, Reform UK Deputy Leader Richard Tice and Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis lead a "march against antisemitism" demonstration in central London on September 7, 2025. (Carlos Jasso/AFP via Getty Images)

Pointing to the U.K., Rodan-Benzaquen said the alliance grew while Jeremy Corbyn was the Labour Party leader. "You have this far left anti-imperialist, anti-colonialist, opposition to American power and, of course, to Israel itself. An alliance with Islamist organizations and movements that sort of adopt a common language, despite the fact that on many topics they are in certain disagreement… They have basically turned themselves from a party that cared about class, that cared about improving (lives), social rights, etcetera, into a party that is basically looking at identity politics and is trying to appeal to certain voters."
She said the red-green alliance is nothing new. "We've seen it for a long time. We've actually seen it in the Islamic Republic of Iran when the Islamic Revolution happened."

Protesters from a number of London universities attend an anti-Israel demonstration on Oct 7, 2025 in London, England. On the same day as people mark the second anniversary of the Hamas attacks on Israel which led to more than 1200 deaths and 251 hostages taken. (Dan Kitwood/Getty Images)

Europe’s Muslim population is estimated to be 45–46 million, up by 15.9% from 2010, based on Pew Research Center projections. That same study revealed the population of European Jewry had fallen to under 1.3 million — down 8% from 2010.
