title: Magazine from 1894 is finally returned to New Hampshire public library
summary: A magazine, checked out and overdue from a New Hampshire library, has finally been returned — perhaps as long as 132 years late.
story: A magazine, checked out and overdue from a New Hampshire library, has finally been returned — perhaps as long as 132 years late.

John Hanson, an 84-year-old Barrington resident, recently strolled into the Concord Public Library to turn in a relatively well cared for edition of “The Century Illustrated Monthly Magazine” from September of 1894.
In theory, Hanson could’ve been on the hook for a $12,055 fine for being 48,220 days overdue. But when Hanson returned it, the library was in the midst of a “fine freeze,” which canceled late fees.
“Yeah, when I saw that, I said to myself, ‘Boy, this would be a good time to bring it back,’” Hanson told NBC News on Tuesday.
The magazine is clearly the property of the Concord Public Library with a bookplate bearing its name and a reminder to readers that this periodical “may be kept for one week.”
Archivist and outreach coordinator Jennifer Needham was working at the circulation desk when Hanson arrived with an envelope in hand.

“‘I have a book to return and I bet you haven’t seen anything like this,’” Needham said, recalling Hanson’s introduction. “I honestly thought it was going to be from the 1980s, 90s, or 2000s. But then he pulled this out and I was like ‘Ooo tell me more!’ ”

Hanson, a Concord native, said he first came upon the periodical during a move from Boscawen to Barrington in 1966. He didn’t know then, and still doesn’t know now, how the work got into his possession.
His parents didn’t have Concord Public Library cards, he said.

Hanson’s late, first wife Carol was a voracious reader and frequent Concord Public Library patron. But he insisted that she, more than anyone else, wouldn’t have allowed a checked out book or magazine to languish for so many years.
“I don’t know, I really don’t know (how the book came into his possession),” Hanson said.
“So I don’t know if it’s something that I got as a gift that was given to me. Or did I pick this up from a pile of free books on the side of the road to read? I honestly don’t know.”
The periodical was typical of its time with a wide variety of writings that included poetry, essays and news.
One topical story in that edition that caught Needham’s eye was about the rise of playgrounds at urban public schools.

“That’s one thing that was really interesting,” the librarian said. “I didn’t know this history, that they were arguing that more city schools should have outdoor spaces for children to play. It sounds like during that time, that just wasn’t a priority. It’s interesting that they would play inside then.”

title: Finneas and other acts exit Ed Sheeran tour in protest of Macklemore being dropped
summary: All of Sheeran’s listed openers have left the tour after New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft worked to have Macklemore removed.
story: Finneas and other musical artists have withdrawn as supporting acts for Ed Sheeran as of Tuesday in protest of Macklemore being dropped from the tour after the rapper says New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft organized a boycott against him.

Macklemore, whose real name is Ben Haggerty, joined Sheeran’s “Loop” tour in New Jersey earlier this month. He made remarks to the Metlife Stadium crowd that included the phrase “Free Palestine” before performing his protest anthem “Hind’s Hall.”
He announced Monday that he was no longer on the tour after Kraft called Sheeran and threatened to cancel Sheeran’s planned tour if Macklemore was still performing.
All of the opening acts listed for Sheeran’s upcoming tour dates have now announced their departures.
Finneas put out a statement saying he decided to withdraw from his upcoming tour dates with Sheeran. He wrote on Instagram that he stands “with Palestine and its people.”
“Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed,” Finneas wrote.

This is not the singer’s first public display of support for Palestinians amid the Israel-Hamas war. He and his younger sister, Billie Eilish, joined fellow celebrities last year to promote a benefit concert to support relief efforts called “Together for Palestine.”
Finneas’ statement came roughly an hour after one of Sheeran’s other openers, Irish singer Aaron Rowe, announced he was dropping out.

Rowe posted his statement to Instagram as well, saying in part that he could not stand by while billionaires silenced voices speaking up against “Israeli genocide” and those who highlight the “savage murder of children.”

“Ed has been a friend to me and has changed my life, I could never thank him enough for this,” Rowe wrote. “But as Irish people we know all too well about genocide, forced famine, and violent occupation.”

A United Nations commission said that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza in findings from an independent inquiry published last year. Israeli government officials have denied the allegations, calling them “distorted and false.”

Beoga, Sheeran’s house band, also said the group was departing the tour. The Irish band described itself as being friends with Sheeran for over 10 years who “never saw ourselves playing in stadiums of that size and that opportunity is not lost on us.”

“It’s important that everyone knows that the real enemy is the zionist lobby,” the band’s statement said. “They have worked tirelessly to silence artists who want to speak freely about a genocide happening before our eyes, for fear of retribution.”
The band’s statement went on to criticize Kraft and express support for Macklemore and his message. It added that the real issue is that Palestinians have been killed.
Beoga’s Instagram post was captioned “Saoirse don Phailistín,” which translates from Irish to “Freedom for Palestine.”

Danish band Lukas Graham issued a statement apologizing to fans but confirming that the group was departing Sheeran’s tour. The statement called on the band’s roots as a small community in Denmark where “speaking your mind was part of everyday life.”
“Having more money didn’t make your opinion worth more than anyone else’s,” the statement said. “Money doesn’t give you the right to own the conversation.”
“We should be able to speak about war, about civilians being killed, about children who deserve to group up,” the band said. “Wherever they live. Whatever flag flies over them.”

Sheeran put out a statement Tuesday morning as backlash against him grew, clarifying that it was not his decision to remove Macklemore from the tour. The “Shape of You” singer said he spent a week trying to build bridges after venues began to reach out to him to say they would pull his shows if Macklemore was still a supporting act.

“I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance, rather than everything that was said,” Sheeran said. “I spoke with venues at length all week to try and build a bridge. One of those people was Robert Kraft.”

But Sheeran says it was his concert promoter who held the contract with Macklemore and the promoter who chose to drop the rapper. He expressed his respect for Macklemore’s “strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes.”

Messina Touring Group, the promoter for Sheeran’s tour, told Rolling Stone Monday that it was informed that multiple venues “will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup.” The statement said cancellations would “impact hundreds of thousands of fans,” confirming that Macklemore would no longer perform on his previously scheduled dates.
The company did not respond to multiple requests for comment from NBC News regarding Macklemore’s removal from the tour.
In his own statement on Monday, Kraft did not deny Macklemore’s accusations.

He said the decision to bar the artist from Gillette Stadium was based on Macklemore’s “recent actions” on stage and “a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community.” Kraft added that the decision was not about trying to stifle Palestinian advocacy or diminishing the suffering of Palestinians.

“I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same — peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate,” Kraft said.

title: FBI Director Kash Patel clashes with Democrats at oversight hearing
summary: Lawmakers pressed FBI Director Kash Patel during a contentious oversight hearing on Tuesday about his leadership of a bureau that has seen massive changes since the start of President Donald Trump’s second term.
story: WASHINGTON — Lawmakers pressed FBI Director Kash Patel during a contentious oversight hearing on Tuesday about his leadership of a bureau that has seen massive changes since the start of President Donald Trump’s second term.

Patel faced scrutiny from Democrats about changes to the FBI’s hiring process amid firings and departures from the bureau since Trump retook office in January 2025. He also faced questions about his use of government aircraft.
As he lashed out at Democrats in the room, an FBI X account launched attacks on several members of the Senate Judiciary Committee.
Following several heated exchanges with Senate Democrats, Patel told Sen. Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, that he “would appreciate it if you concluded this hearing.”

Sen. Dick Durbin, the Illinois Democrat who is not seeking re-election this year, noted this will likely be his last FBI oversight hearing until retirement and said he was “disappointed” the Senate Judiciary Committee “has stood by” since Trump retook office in January 2025. “I look forward to a day, hopefully in the very near future, when this committee will fulfill its duty to hold Director Patel accountable for his leadership,” Durbin said.
Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., compared Patel to a “thug” and said he was using the FBI “to go after reporters” and stonewalling members of Congress who had questions about his oversight of the FBI.

Democrats also questioned Patel over reports of an investigation into leaks that resulted in a story in The Atlantic focusing on concerns about his personal behavior. In April, Patel filed a $250 million lawsuit against the magazine over the story that made allegations about his drinking, with Patel’s team saying the FBI director “does not drink to excess.”
Add to Google
Add to Google

Republican Senate Judiciary members largely praised the FBI director. They discussed with Patel how the FBI was handling what they claimed was “weaponization” of law enforcement during the prior administrations. Republicans have complained former special counsel Jack Smith obtained records of legislators’ phone calls and accused him of spying, though Smith had obtained records of legislators’ communications with members of the executive branch because they turned up during the investigation into Jan. 6 and Trump’s efforts to overturn the 2020 election.

Patel’s FBI has overseen the firing of numerous FBI employees who were involved in prior investigations into Trump, including individuals involved in the 2022 search of Mar-a-Lago that has been a particular focus for Trump.

Joe diGenova, the 81-year-old Trump loyalist who had been heading a “grand conspiracy” probe targeting former law enforcement officials involved in Trump investigations, told NBC News that Patel had been “absolutely superb in supporting our investigation.” DiGenova resigned last week after a conflict with Justice Department leadership about the direction of the investigation.
If Democrats take control of the House or Senate, Patel’s FBI is expected to face increased scrutiny and investigations.

title: Hyrox co-founder apologizes after athlete allowed to continue despite defecating on herself
summary: Professional athlete Joanna Wietrzyk was seen on video and in photographs running and using shared fitness equipment with feces running down her legs.
story: The international indoor sports competition Hyrox apologized after an incident in Beijing where a runner was allowed to continue a race after soiling herself during the event.

Professional athlete Joanna Wietrzyk finished and won the competition on Saturday, which consists of running and high-intensity exercises. The athlete was seen on video and in photographs racing and using shared fitness equipment with feces running down her legs.

Competitors alternate between running a kilometer and performing exercises at workout stations, including sled pushes and pulls, burpees, rowing, lunges while carrying sandbags. Wietrzyk holds a world record in the Hyrox women’s solo event.

Hyrox co-founder Moritz Fürste issued a statement Sunday on social media apologizing “to all that were directly or indirectly affected, as well as to everyone who felt like we did not handle the situation like we should have.”
“HYROX made a mistake by not reacting immediately during the race,” he wrote. “In the end it is my job to foresee these potential incidents — and I did not.”
Fürste said Hyrox made changes to its rules and procedures for the event as a result of the incident, but did not elaborate on what those changes were.
“As of this moment, there are new rules and procedures in place to prevent situations like this from happening again,” he said.

In another statement on social media, the company said: “As our sport continues to evolve we are encountering new and increasingly complex situations that challenge us and where additional clarity is needed.” The statement has since been removed.

“We ask our athletes to push themselves to the highest levels. At times, they will go beyond what even we thought was possible,” the brand said. “That courage, resilience and refusal to give in are precisely what makes elite athletes so extraordinary. Our role is to give them the right framework and the right boundaries within which they can compete, perform and express themselves at their very best.”

The brand said it has “clear biocontaminant and medical procedures in place. In this instance, an unforeseen situation arose in which protocols designed for elite competition and mass participation became blurred, creating ambiguity in how they were applied and understood.”

“We recognise that this can understandably lead to frustration, questions and strong views within our community,” the statement said. “Those concerns are legitimate and, as organisers, we must be prepared to hear them, examine what happened and take responsibility for continuing to improve.”
Hyrox did not immediately respond to requests for comment on why the post was taken down or what specific policy changes were made in response to Saturday’s race.
Wietrzyk did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

According to The Guardian, Wietrzyk posted and later deleted an image of herself to her Instagram story from what appeared to be a hospital bed, that read, “Go hard or go home … a win is a win. In all seriousness, thank you for all the support. I’ll be back soon.”

title: ‘I’m not going to be a Republican!’: John Fetterman promises, again, not to defect
summary: Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., insisted he won’t become a Republican, showing frustration with the ongoing questions about his intentions.
story: WASHINGTON — Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., insisted Tuesday he won’t become a Republican, showing frustration with the ongoing questions about his intentions.
Sen. Fetterman says he will not switch to Republican party
“I’m not going to be a Republican!” Fetterman said to reporters on Capitol Hill, raising his voice and shaking his head. “If I turn a Republican, then I’ll be a liar.”

“My name is not on the ballot. Like, chill and wait for the midterm here,” he added. “I’ve always been a Democrat. It’s like, no matter how many times I say that, I’m still getting asked just getting into the elevator.”

Fetterman, first elected in 2022, has grown increasingly distant from his party, mainly over his impassioned and unyielding defense of Israel and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He’s a regular guest on Fox News, where he gets asked about left-wing members of the Democratic Party and readily whacks them.
Those positions and actions have drawn significant attention on Fetterman as a Democrat, but would become far less remarkable if he defected to the GOP.

Fetterman sparked the speculation in mid-July when he opened the door to leaving the Democratic Party if it “officially” became “anti-Israel” in the party platform. As Republicans invited him to defect, he wondered aloud to NBC News days later whether Democrats still want him in the party. In response, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., called Fetterman “a very good member of Congress” and one Democrats respect.

The speculation arose again last week when Fetterman made a video appearance at the two-day Republican midterm convention in Dallas to introduce his “friend,” Sen. David McCormick, R-Pa. Fetterman issued a statement shortly after that saying he won’t switch parties if Democrats capture Senate control in November.

His seat comes up for re-election in 2028, and Fetterman’s prospects of winning renomination as a Democrat are rapidly fading. A New York Times/Philadelphia Inquirer/Siena poll last month found Fetterman’s approval rating among Democrats was just 22%, having fallen precipitously from 74% in May 2024.

Yet, despite his rising approval rating among Pennsylvania Republicans in the same poll, his prospects of winning a GOP primary may be even more remote. Fetterman would have to defend his wide array of liberal positions — on matters such as expanding health care access, raising the federal minimum wage, supporting LGBTQ rights and championing legal abortion.

On Tuesday, Fetterman ignored questions about a recently created X account reportedly run by his former staffers who have turned against him. He also declined to comment on a recent Wall Street Journal report detailing examples of Fetterman showing a lack of interest in doing the job of a senator, citing interviews with more than a dozen former staffers and lawmakers. Neither he nor his office commented for that story, but Fetterman called its reporting “smears” in a statement to CNN.
One person who was quick to defend Fetterman was McCormick.

“These stories are the latest example of outrageously disloyal staff and forces on the Left using anonymous leaks to cancel my friend John Fetterman,” he said on X. “They hate that he is an independent thinker who refuses to fall into line so they want to silence him.”

title: Iran war driving up inflation for Americans, CBO report says
summary: The Congressional Budget Office estimates inflation will continue to rise in the first quarter of next year.
story: WASHINGTON — The war with Iran is driving up inflation, and borrowing costs may increase for Americans, according to a new report released Tuesday by the Congressional Budget Office.

The report found the war was responsible for more than one-third of the increase in inflation this year, and inflation will likely continue to grow in the first quarter of next year. The CBO specifically blames the war for more than 40% of inflation during the second quarter of 2026 and an estimated half a percentage point of higher inflation during the first quarter of 2027. Interest rates are likely to rise as a result, making borrowing costlier, the report found.

Interest rates are likely to keep rising as a result, making borrowing more costly, the report found. The rate on the typical 30-year mortgage was under 6% before the war started; it was at 7.22% on Tuesday, according to Mortgage News Daily. Wall Street, likewise, expects the Federal Reserve to raise its key interest rate Wednesday in a bid to tamp down inflation.

The main driver of increased inflation is fewer oil and natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, the CBO report says. The average price of a gallon of gasoline in the U.S. is up 45% since the beginning of the war, hitting $4.32 as of Tuesday. Diesel, which is essential to the economy as it fuels farm equipment and other commercial vehicles, has increased 66%, to a record $6.26.
The Congressional Budget Office is a nonpartisan federal agency controlled by Congress that conducts analysis related to the federal budget and the economy.
The estimate comes a day after the Pentagon’s watchdog found the Iran war resulted in a shortfall of U.S. munitions and “bottlenecks” in supply chains.

The CBO report estimates it will be five years before the Pentagon is able to replace munitions expended during the war, which it estimates had cost roughly $38 billion as of Aug. 1. That cost estimate does not include the price tag for repairing damage Iran inflicted on “hundreds of buildings and structures at U.S. bases” in the Middle East.
The Pentagon didn’t cooperate with requests from CBO, according to the agency.

“For 47 years, American Presidents and countless other world leaders talked about the threat posed by Iran, but no one had the courage to address it,” White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said in a statement. “President Trump took decisive action to ensure that Iran could never harm our homeland, our troops, or our allies again. The United States Military has more than enough munitions, ammo, and stockpiles to serve all of the Commander-in-Chief’s strategic goals and beyond.”

One of the reasons the CBO says it could not estimate the cost of damage to U.S. military bases and other facilities in the region is that the Defense Department hasn’t shared “information about the value of damaged or destroyed equipment and property” with the office or what repairs the Pentagon plans to make, the funding for which could in part be picked up by the countries where the facilities are located.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., called for an end to the war in a statement, describing it as “a one-two punch that’s burning a hole in Americans’ pockets and burning a hole in our munitions supply, hurting our military readiness.”

The report estimated it would cost $13.1 billion to replace missile defense interceptors alone, and the overall cost to replace munitions expended through Aug. 1 would be $21.7 billion. It will take roughly $2 billion to $3 billion per month to maintain the war’s status quo, and more if the conflict escalates, the report found.

title: Pennsylvania teen dies from measles complications, health officials report
summary: A fourth death has been linked to measles in Pennsylvania, the state health department said Tuesday.
story: A fourth death has been linked to measles in Pennsylvania, the state health department said Tuesday.
All four deaths have been reported in the last month, as Pennsylvania’s measles outbreak continues to grow. They are the first deaths associated with measles in the state in 35 years.
In all of last year, the U.S. recorded three measles deaths.
Pennsylvania’s health department said in a news release Tuesday that the two people who died most recently were from Jefferson and Mifflin counties. Both were unvaccinated, the department said.

The Mifflin County coroner said Tuesday that an 18-year-old resident died “due to complications of measles,” specifically, a rare and severe neurological condition that causes inflammation in the brain. The Jefferson County resident was a 40-year-old woman with asthma and severe lung disease who died on Saturday, the county coroner previously reported.

The two deaths in Lancaster County were in infants: a newborn who died shortly after birth and a 6-week-old. The county coroner has said he believes measles was only the cause of death for the 6-week-old baby. In the case of the newborn, the coroner said he found evidence of the measles virus in the infant’s lung tissue but considered the cause of death to be an internal hemorrhage and “traumatic rupture” of the spleen.

The first dose of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine is typically given at around 1 year, so neither infant had been eligible to receive it. Two doses offer 97% protection against measles, usually for life (the second is given at around age 5).

The Pennsylvania health department considers a death to be “measles associated” if there is clinical evidence of a measles infection, a positive laboratory test and if the death occurred within 30 days of symptoms starting. It also takes into account the person’s medical records and whether they were exposed to measles prior to their death.

The department said in a press release that the two latest deaths were linked to measles after rigorous investigations involving the county coroners’ offices. The two infant deaths involved similar investigations, the department said.

Nearly 700 measles cases have been reported in Pennsylvania this year; 133 people have been hospitalized. State officials have tied the outbreak to falling vaccination rates. Nationwide, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed 3,294 measles cases, including 267 hospitalizations, as of Sept. 10.

The CDC has not yet confirmed any of the deaths reported in Pennsylvania and states on its website that it does not have any death records from 2026 indicating measles is the underlying cause. Traditionally, the CDC has accepted death reports like Pennsylvania’s from state health departments; the discrepancy represents a significant departure from the way the agency has operated in the past.
CDC Director Erica Schwartz said Monday that Pennsylvania, unlike other states with measles outbreaks, had not requested the CDC’s assistance.

However, the Pennsylvania health department said it “maintains a strong working relationship with the professional staff at the CDC.” It also said it submits death records to the CDC’s National Center for Health Statistics “daily,” including for the recent measles-associated deaths.

Last month, the deaths of the infants in Lancaster County ignited a flurry of misinformation online, as well as political sparring between Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Shapiro accused Kennedy of spreading falsehoods about vaccines, while Kennedy suggested the deaths may have been “fabricated” and that Shapiro was seeking to profit from them politically.

Anti-vaccine activists commonly argue that testing positive for measles does not necessarily mean someone died from the virus if a secondary illness or injury was involved. However, doctors say measles is still the underlying cause in many of those cases, since patients would not have died otherwise.
The father of the newborn in Lancaster County told NBC News the baby had been born prematurely and that his mother had measles. Premature birth is a known complication of measles during pregnancy.

Measles can also cause the spleen to enlarge, which raises the risk of rupture. The Lancaster County coroner said he did not find evidence that the newborn’s spleen had been enlarged; however, that can be difficult to detect in an autopsy.

title: Trump’s handpicked Kennedy Center board again votes to close venue, calling it ‘unsafe’
summary: The board voted shortly after a federal judge rejected its latest effort to add the president’s name to the building’s facade.
story: President Donald Trump’s handpicked Kennedy Center board voted Tuesday to immediately shutter the performing arts center, citing its “dire” financial and structural shape.
The vote came shortly after a federal judge in Washington rejected the board’s latest effort to add Trump’s name to the building’s facade. A spokesperson for the center said it would appeal.
Trump said on social media after the vote that renovations wouldn’t happen unless his name was added to the building.

“The closing will take place immediately, however, the Renovation and Reconstruction, which is a very large and complex job, cannot begin until such time as the D.C. Circuit rules on the Board’s approved name,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “If the ruling is a negative one, which it should not be, and is not overturned by the U.S. Supreme Court, the Reconstruction and the Renovation of The Kennedy Center will not take place.”

“In the meantime, 17 Million Dollars, raised by President Trump, has been put into The Kennedy Center account to keep it afloat,” he added. Congress appropriated $250 million for the project last year.
The board had cited a partial ceiling collapse in the center’s Grand Foyer this month as evidence that the center needed to be immediately closed for repairs.

A construction consultant and the center’s director “consider the main building to be unsafe for continued occupancy, and anticipate further risk to the public and employees if the building is not immediately closed and renovations begun,” the board said in a draft resolution to close the center for two years.

It was the third time since February that the board has voted to close the center for renovations for two years. Rep. Joyce Beatty, D-Ohio, an ex officio board member, has challenged those efforts in court, saying the board hadn’t done its due diligence before it decided it needed to close the venue.
The center was initially scheduled to close July 5.

Attorneys for the board have said the legal action has kept them from doing necessary repairs, but the judge presiding over the case noted at a hearing Tuesday — as he had previously — that his earlier order preventing full closure allowed for emergency repairs.

Trump, who was elected chairman last year by the board he appointed, joined the closed-door meeting virtually and spent several minutes criticizing both Beatty and the judge who blocked his name from being added to the facade, according to a source who dialed into the Zoom meeting and who opposes the closure.

That person described Trump as getting into a shouting match with Beatty, whom he blasted as an “obstructionist” who didn’t know how to get things done. Beatty countered that Trump was unprofessional, and at one point each accused the other of incompetence, the source said.

During the tirade, Trump also suggested without evidence that the judge, Christopher Cooper, is compromised because his wife, an attorney, represented former President Joe Biden, the source said. Trump also suggested there was something untoward about the judge’s wife’s not using her husband’s last name, the source said.

Attorneys for the center are expected to ask the judge to lift his block on closing the center this week. A source familiar with Beatty’s legal strategy said her attorneys will oppose the move and argue that the repairs can be done without shutting down the center.

In a separate resolution that was originally scheduled to be taken up Tuesday, as well, the Kennedy Center said that it “is in a dire financial position” and facing potential bankruptcy after it “exhausted its fiscal resources” — and that only Trump can rescue it.
The board had said that to do so, he would have to be recognized for his efforts on the exterior of the building.

“The Kennedy Center is in such a precarious fiscal position that it will not be able to support its payroll obligations, nor routine maintenance contracts within a matter of weeks,” said the draft resolution, which was made public in a court filing. “While actively considering alternative means of fiscal survival, President Trump has offered to step in and raise the necessary funds to keep the Center from bankruptcy during its much needed renovation.”

“With certain fiscal collapse within weeks, the board seeks to determine what recognition and acknowledgement will comply” with the judge’s earlier order banning the center from being renamed the Donald J. Trump and John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts.
The board didn’t vote on the resolution at the meeting because members said they needed to focus on the closure issue.

The trustees had voted last month to instead add the words “renovated and restored by President Donald J. Trump” to the building and to rename the center’s grounds President Donald J. Trump Plaza by Sept. 8. The new draft resolution offered numerous similar suggestions.
In a ruling issued just ahead of the board vote, Cooper, the judge, found the effort to add Trump’s name to the facade in a different way was also illegal.

“Simply put, Defendants cannot install memorials for President Trump or anyone or anything else at the Kennedy Center without Congress’s blessing. The board resolution bucks a federal court order and a statute Congress enacted,” Cooper said.
He also noted the board’s threat about fundraising — and its claim that the center might need to be razed if Trump’s repair plan isn’t followed — with skepticism.

The “government offered ‘no proof that current or future donations hinge on President Trump’s name being on the building’ and ‘no competent evidence that removing the Trump name would prevent the Center from fulfilling its artistic mission, as it has done for the last sixty years,’” he wrote.
Instead, Cooper suggested, the opposite could be true.

“The renaming of the Center coincided with declines in revenue and contributions, as artists cancelled performances, the Washington National Opera ended its 50-year residency, and ticket sales and viewership of the Kennedy Center Honors broadcast dropped precipitously. The Board also has access to the $257 million that Congress appropriated for necessary capital improvements,” he wrote, but that’s “beside the point for present purposes.”
And while cultural institutions often honor big donors by naming buildings or features after them, Cooper said, “Congress had other ideas for the Kennedy Center.”

“It limited such memorials and donor recognitions to discrete (and discreet) areas, so as not to detract from the Center’s function as an ongoing memorial to President Kennedy. The current Board’s apparent disagreement with that approach does not change the law,” he wrote.

Cooper said he could “not license a violation of those authorities under threat that some unidentified donors will withhold their largesse if the Board is not allowed to have its way. It can even less reward a decision by Board members, including the Chair, to curb the Center’s fundraising efforts because they cannot abide statutory restrictions on displaying his name.”

Beatty praised Cooper’s ruling in a statement, saying: “The law is extremely clear: The John F. Kennedy Center is named for President Kennedy — and no one else. But President Trump is holding the Kennedy Center hostage unless he can put his name on this sacred memorial.”
“This unlawfulness is as breathtaking as it is wrong, and it needs to stop,” she said.
Her attorneys, Norm Eisen of Democracy Defenders Action and Nathaniel Zelinsky of Washington Litigation Group, said in a joint statement, “Legal sanity has once again prevailed over Trump’s vanity.”

Roma Daravi, vice president for public relations at the Kennedy Center, said in a statement, “We intend to appeal today’s Court ruling and move forward with recognizing Chairman President Trump’s historic contributions to the revitalization of America’s Cultural Center.”

title: Talking Shop with Ciara Miller ahead of her ‘Dancing with the Stars’ debut
summary: Summer House star Ciara Miller is competing on Dancing with the Stars season 35. These are her rehearsal, recovery and performance essentials from Nexxus, Bala and more.
story: Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys.

She took the Hamptons by storm from the moment she joined the cast of Bravo’s Summer House. She held down the fort in Fiji while hosting Love Island: Aftersun. She modeled in campaigns for some of the biggest brands in the world. And now, Ciara Miller is tackling a new challenge: competing for the Mirrorball Trophy on season 35 of Dancing with the Stars, which premiers tonight at 8 p.m. ET on ABC/Disney+.

“I’m definitely getting a run for my money,” says Miller, who told me that she’s wanted to do the show for years. “It’s such an experience for growth. I danced growing up, but I did ballet and hip hop and jazz and stuff. This is such a different sector of dance that I wanted to experience.”

Miller’s partner this season is Brandon Armstrong, a multi-season DWTS pro. She says he’s been a great teacher and choreographer, but she’s putting her mark on performances, too. “Brandon is in charge of one thing: the dancing,” says Miller. “I’m in charge of everything else. We have creative calls where we can be as involved or not involved as we want, and I’m involved, even down to his outfits.”

Before Miller’s first live performance, I talked to her about what she’s using to recover after hours-long rehearsals and products she swears by on the dance floor. And, of course, because she’s the first Summer House cast member to be in the ballroom, I had to ask: If she could cast any of her other housemates on Dancing with the Stars, who would it be? “Kyle [Cooke] would be number one on my Mount Rushmore,” says Miller. “I tried to teach him a pose, and I would really enjoy seeing Kyle attempting to learn any type of dance at all.”
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Bala Bangles Wrist & Ankle Weights

One of the most useful purchases Miller has made during Dancing with the Stars rehearsals so far is Bala Bangles. “I just got these arm weights because a lot of my moves this first week are in frame, and my arms look like chicken wings instead of an elegant bird,” she says. “So I was like, okay, what can keep me mindful of keeping my arms up? These weights are how I’ve been training my arms.” She got a pink pair and tries to keep them on for the entirety of each practice session.
Dr. Teal’s Pure Epsom Salt Sooth & Sleep with Lavender

Miller isn’t shy about sharing what the hardest part about being on Dancing with the Stars is: “I am not flexible anymore, so I really have to stretch,” she says. “My back, my neck… I’m so sore everywhere.” She’s taking recovery very seriously, starting with hot baths. “I’m soaking in a bathtub almost every day for at least 20 minutes. It’s essential,” says Miller. “I’m living for Dr. Teal’s epsom salt. I’ve got the sleepytime one, I’ve got the one for muscle recovery; I’ve got all the things.”
Currentbody LED Red Light Therapy Face Mask

To continue winding down after her bath, Miller puts on her favorite red light therapy mask from Currentbody. “It’s flexible, so it can fit into small spaces, and I didn’t have to worry about crushing it when I was traveling, which was nice,” she says, referring to her recent move from New York City to Los Angeles. “I use it to relax and treat my skin, and I’m incorporating getting massages, too, because I need to get better about recouping. But at home, it’s the simple things. I obviously love my bed, and I love a Salt & Stone candle — it’s one of my favorite things to have in my room.”
Homedics Bubble Mate Foot Spa

Miller isn’t just dancing for hours a day — she’s doing so while wearing heels. “You’ve got to break your shoes in and get used to them,” she says. “I’ve honestly been doing good so far and wearing socks with them. I’m the type of person where wearing a new shoe sometimes almost stresses me out, unless it’s for the look. But in this case, I knew I had to get acquainted with them early.”

One of her go-to ways to care for achy feet is by using a foot spa. “I’m bringing back the pedicure bath things that I was like, I haven’t seen this thing in 20 years,” she says. “But I got one on Amazon, and I would say it’s one of my best purchases of 2026.”
Solely Organic Mango Fruit Jerky

As for Miller’s favorite thing to nosh on pre-, post- and during rehearsal? “Fruit — I don’t like eating a heavy meal beforehand,” she says. “I love Solely fruit jerky. I swear by it and it helps spike my blood sugar if I’m feeling a little bit eh. It’s healthy and really great on the go.” There’s always Celcius in her refrigerator too, a brand she recently worked with to launch its Spritz Vibe beverage.
Nexxus Air Shape Workable Hold Texture Spray

Miller immediately stocked her DWTS trailer with Nexxus hair care when she got access to it. She’s been working with the brand throughout the year, and says its products continuously fit into different aspects of her life.

“With Dancing with the Stars, we’re going to be in several different types of hairstyles, so you really need something that’s going to withstand the test of time from the wee hours of the morning to at night when we’re live on TV,” says Miller. “We all know I’m a glam girl — I love my glam, and obviously I’m going to be focused on it. But when it comes down to it, I need reliable products that I know are going to hold me through so my attention is on my dancing entirely.”

Her favorite Nexxus product is the Air Shape Workable Hold Texture Spray. “I like volume. I like big hair. I want to pull it out and make it even bigger,” says Miller. “I’m a texture girl. And obviously I need a firm hairspray to hold it all in place, too.”
Why trust NBC Selected?

I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who writes our Talking Shop series, interviewing people like Paris Hilton, Maureen Kelly, Lindsay Hubbard and Chase Crawford. To write this article, I talked to Summer House star Ciara Miller about the products she’s relying on while rehearsing for and competing in season 35 of Dancing with the Stars.

title: Here’s how to pick a Kindle that actually fits how you read (and your budget)
summary: We’ve used Amazon Kindles for more than a decade. Here’s everything you need to know about each model, and which one is right for you.
story: Amazon Kindle has been one of our favorite e-readers for years — some of our editors have actually been using them as far back as 2012. (The first Kindle came out in 2007). If you’re unfamiliar, they’re known for being lightweight, simple to use and make reading while on the go a lot more pleasant than using your phone or a tablet that wasn’t made for reading.

Now, nearly 20 years after the release of its first model, Amazon has a few versions, each with slight variations that can make it confusing to know which one is right for you, especially when most of them look the same at a glance. I’ve tested different Kindle devices for years, and explain the key differences below so you don’t spend your money only to find that you prefer a different option. Here’s how to pick the best Kindle for your needs.

Best overallAmazon Kindle Paperwhite (2024)$undefined$199.99AmazonLearn more

Best for note takingAmazon Kindle Scribe (2024)$399.99$499.99AmazonLearn more
Which is the best Kindle model to buy?

There are a handful of different Amazon Kindle models to choose from and which one will be best for you depends on your needs and the features you value. NBC Selected editors have tested nearly all of them, and they each have key differences that help you decide which one to buy.
Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (2024)
Adjustable light hueLong battery lifeWaterproof
Adjustable light hue
Long battery life
Waterproof
Power button is at the bottom
Power button is at the bottom

The Kindle Paperwhite is the go-to model for many NBC Selected staffers, myself included. Like all Kindles, it has a glare-free screen that makes it easy to read outside, even under bright sunlight. What makes the Paperwhite our favorite is its long battery life (the longest of any Kindle) and adjustable hue — you can change the tone of the screen light to be warmer or cooler. The warmer hue in particular makes it easier on the eyes when reading in dark rooms.
I pair mine with a Kindle Paperwhite fabric case — it’s soft and slim, and automatically turns the screen off when closed.
Amazon Kindle (2024)
Compact and lightweightCompetitive price
Compact and lightweight
Competitive price
Less adjustable screenNot waterproof
Less adjustable screen
Not waterproof

The plain Amazon Kindle, no tagline, is the model to get if you want the lowest-priced option. Despite its lower cost, using it is more or less a similar experience as any other Kindle — it uses the same software and same Kindle bookstore. Reading books and listening to audiobooks feels very similar on this (and every) Kindle.

It’s also the smallest and lightest Kindle at well under a half pound — the weight of an average-size orange. It doesn’t have the Paperwhite’s adjustable light hue and it isn’t waterproof so if you like to read at the beach or pool this may not be the one for you, but while you’re otherwise reading and swiping through your favorite book, you might not notice much of a difference.
Amazon Kindle Colorsoft
Color displayAdjustable light hueWaterproof
Color display
Adjustable light hue
Waterproof
Less contrast for text
Less contrast for text

Amazon’s first color e-reader, the Kindle Colorsoft is a great fit for anyone reading a lot of colorful comic books and graphic novels. It also makes highlighted text more noticeable and useful than on black and white Kindles.
Outside of the color screen, the Kindle Colorsoft is most similar to the Kindle Paperwhite: It has the same adjustable light hue, waterproof design and seven-inch screen size.

It isn’t the best option if you plan on mostly reading regular, black and white books — the screen has slightly less contrast, so black and white text looks a little less crisp than on the Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite.
Amazon Kindle Scribe (2024)
Allows writing and note takingStylus includedLong battery life
Allows writing and note taking
Stylus included
Long battery life
Most expensive optionLarger and heavier than others
Most expensive option
Larger and heavier than others

If you want a Kindle that can also be your notetaking companion, the Kindle Scribe is what you’re looking for. Former NBC Selected production coordinator Kelsey Fredricks tested it for two months and loved how responsive the screen was for taking notes. It comes with a stylus that’s smooth, comfortable to use and attaches to the side of the device with magnets for convenient storage.
You can sort your notes and documents on the e-reader and send them to your phone, computer, email or printer easily, says Fredricks.

The Scribe is larger than other Kindles, which makes it more comfortable for note taking but a bit bulkier in your hands and bag. At nearly a pound, it’s also a much heavier model. This model has an LED screen that allows you to read in a dark room, though there is a version without the light, too. You can read more in our Amazon Kindle Scribe review.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Is it worth it to buy a Kindle in 2026?

An Amazon Kindle is a book-sized device that uses an electronic-ink screen to display text, which simulates the appearance of ink on paper, says Nick Tanzi, assistant director of the South Huntington Public Library. E-ink screens are more comfortable to look at for long periods of time than smartphone or tablet screens, in our experience. They are also free of glare and reflections, which make them easy to read outside in the sun, unlike a smartphone or tablet. You can adjust the brightness of the screen, change from light mode to dark mode and, with some models, change the warmth or cool hue of the light.
E-ink screens also use significantly less battery power than other kinds of screens — it’s part of the reason Kindle devices can go so long without needing a recharge.

Amazon Kindle devices connect to Wi-Fi so you can browse the Amazon Kindle store, where you can purchase and download e-books and audiobooks. Your Kindle can also typically sync to public library apps like Libby, so your loans will appear on your Kindle too. So investing in a Kindle is worth it if you’re an avid reader and prefer to have all your titles in one device, giving you several options anytime you like.
Is it worth getting a Kindle for kids?

Aside from the Kindle Scribe, all of the Kindles above come in kid-versions: The Kindle Kids, Kindle Paperwhite Kids and Kindle Colorsoft Kids. They are the same device as the “adult” version, but come with no ads, a protective cover and six months of Amazon Kids+, the brand’s age three to 12-book subscription service. If your child likes to read or you want to encourage them to, a Kindle Kids device is a worthwhile investment.
What is the Kindle Signature Edition?

Amazon also makes pricier versions of its Kindle Paperwhite and a Kindle Colorsoft, called Signature Editions. The Signature Edition models have more internal storage (32GB, up from 16GB), automatically adjust the screen brightness when you are in a bright or dark space, come without ads on the lockscreen and support Qi wireless charging.

For most people, I don’t think the Signature Edition is worth the extra cost — I have never come close to running out of storage on a Kindle, and the device has such good battery life that wired charging has never been an inconvenience.
What’s the difference between a tablet and a Kindle?

A tablet is more phone than e-reader: it can run hundreds of apps, including streaming platforms and video games. A Kindle is optimized for reading, and can’t do nearly as much as a tablet on purpose. Devices like the Boox Palma 2 toe the line between phone, tablet and e-reader.
Frequently asked questions

It depends on the size and type of book. An average e-book file is around 2MB, in my experience, and most Kindles come with 16GB of internal storage: that means it can store thousands of e-books easily. Be aware that graphic novels, cookbooks and comic books take up significantly more storage space.

If you have an active Prime Membership, Prime Reading is free, and allows you to access several e-books, audiobooks, magazines, and comic books at no cost. You do still have to pay for your Kindle device separately, and not all titles you are looking for will be free. However, Amazon often offers deals on Kindle Unlimited during Amazon Prime Day, Prime Big Deal Days and other sales events.

You can use your public library card to borrow e-books, audiobooks and other material free of charge, just like going to the library in-person. I use and love the library app Libby, which makes it easy to sync borrowed e-books from my phone to my Kindle.
Meet our e-reader expert

At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest.
Nick Tanzi is the assistant director of the South Huntington Public Library.

title: Does Taylor Swift’s ‘SVU’ Skit Have a Secret Message to Her Fans?
summary: What could “saccharide, Aries, from the vineyard, north or south” really mean? Taylor Swift’s “SVU” skit at the Emmys has her fans speculating about Easter Eggs.
story: “Saccharide. Aries. From the vineyard. North or south.”

These arbitrary phrases have left Swifties everywhere with dozens of questions after the Emmy Awards, the main one being: Is Taylor Swift the mastermind her fans know her to be, or did she just send them on a wild goose chase?

Clues point to the former. But first, let’s rewind for those who need it: Mariska Hargitay had hosted the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards on Sept. 14 and had tapped Swift, her friend and longtime “Law & Order: SVU” fan, to appear in an “SVU” parody skit that aired during the telecast.
The pre-taped sketch features Hargitay, Ice-T, Kelli Giddish, Peter Scanavino and more actors playing their characters from the crime drama. Their case to crack: Will Taylor Swift attend the Emmys?

Hargitay, as Olivia Benson, brought up as evidence Swift’s love of Easter eggs. She wheeled out a crime board filled with clues as each person took turns suggesting why certain nominees and shows pointed toward Swift making a surprise appearance.
Suddenly, a crime board was wheeled away to reveal Swift was standing in the precinct.
“Hey guys, this isn’t adding up,” she said while wearing a gray suit and holding a coffee mug.
Ice-T rebuffed her input. “And who asked you, rookie?” he said.
She replied, “Our perp has a clear M.O. A lot of this doesn’t fit the pattern, and I don’t think everything is a clue.”
“It is to the Swifties,” Hargitay quickly replied.
“I think what we’re going to be looking for is hiding in plain sight,” Swift replied.
She then panned and spoke directly to the camera: “Saccharide. Aries. From the vineyard. North or south.”
“What did you just say?” Hargitay asked her.
“I didn’t say anything,” Swift said with a shrug.

While the sketch wraps by cracking its case — Swift won’t be at the Emmys because she’ll be busy supporting husband Travis Kelce at the Chiefs season opener — the meaning of Swift’s spoken message is still a mystery.
Swifties of course know that nothing is ever that simple when it comes to the singer. They immediately began dissecting the skit on social media, seeing if they could decode a secret message.
What could it mean? Well, the Emmys executive producers have confirmed that the words have some type of significance because they were specifically chosen by Swift.

After the Emmys, executive producers Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzon-Clay from Jesse Collins Entertainment, and NBCUniversal live events and specials exec VP Jen Neal, spoke with reporters and explained how they pulled off the sketch.
“Taylor loved the script and she had some thoughts and we worked that in,” Collins told reporters, according to Variety.
One of Swift’s notes was to add Easter eggs, Collins revealed.
“She wanted them to be really official. And correct,” Rouzan-Clay shared.

As always, Swifties are on the case, and they might’ve already cracked it. Many shared their theories on social media that the sketch pointed to Swift releasing the long-awaited “Taylor’s Versions” from her debut and “Reputation” albums.
One Swiftie said on X that Ice-T’s “rookie” line and Aries, the first astrological sign, reference her self-titled first album.

Another zoomed in on the crime board and noticed a Post-it note that read “Is it TV?” adding more fuel to the fire. The board also had a heart similar to the one Swift used to draw on the back of her hand during the early days of her career.
Beneath the post, one X user replied, “Olivia said ‘the answer has been TV this whole time’ also.”
But others were more convinced that “Reputation (Taylor’s Version)” is on the way.

“I believe Debut TV is next but to add fuel to the Rep TV fire (no pun intended), if you go all the way back to the Karma MV in the Reputation scene Taylor wears the ram mask and the ram is the Aries zodiac animal,” one tweeted.
Over on Reddit, the speculation continued.
“I’m putting in my guess now — these are Rep vault track titles,” one suggested.
And one fan had a wild but plausible idea.
“OMG GUYS THERES TWO BOARDS!!! TWO!!” they said. “We are getting both Debut and Rep.”
Looks like we’ll have to wait for Swift’s next message to see what other tricks she has up her sleeve.

title: All About Keri Russell and Matthew Rhys’ Relationship, From How They Met to ‘The Americans’
summary: On screen, Keri Russell and Matthew Rhys paired a pair of married Russian spies living undercover in “The Americans,” which ran from 2013 to 2018 on FX.
story: On screen, Keri Russell and Matthew Rhys paired a pair of married Russian spies living undercover in “The Americans,” which ran from 2013 to 2018 on FX.
Off screen, the “Felicity” star and the Welsh actor were falling in love.

While “The Americans” was still airing in 2017, the couple spoke to People about making their relationship work. Russell said a bit of “alone time,” since they spend so much time together. Plus, Rhys said, “she has the patience of a saint, so that helps.”
Rhys and Russell turned heads at the 2026 Emmys, where they appeared on the red carpet together because they were both nominated for acting awards.

Russell was nominated for outstanding lead actress in a drama series for her role as Kate Wyler in “The Diplomat,” which she lost, and Rhys was nominated — and won — for both outstanding lead actor in a comedy series as Tom Loftis in “Widow’s Bay” and outstanding lead actor in a limited or anthology series or movie as Nile Jarvis in “The Beast in Me.”

But when the trophies where handed out, Rhys still felt that Russell came out on top. In a video captured by the Associated Press, he praised his longtime partner for her more measured approach to awards season: After joking that he tends to brag about his wins more than Russell, who is always supportive of her competitors, Rhys quipped, “She’s always really the winner, if I’m perfectly honest.”
Here’s what to know about their roughly 13-year-long relationship.
They Met Long Before “The Americans”
During a joint appearance on “Watch What Happens Live“ in 2017, Rhys and Russell recalled the first time they met.
Rhys said it was a “a very long, long time ago” — back when he was 26 years old.
“I very drunkenly asked her for her number when she was a young single slip of a thing,” Rhys said.
They had met after a “kickball party,” Russell said. The conversation happened in a parking lot after Russell asked Rhys to open up a beer for her.
Rhys gave more of the story in a 2023 appearance on “Watch What Happens Live.” He left her a drunken voice mail — to which she didn’t respond.
Their Romance Rekindled on ‘The Americans’
But “it took a while,” Rhys said of their love story on “Watch What Happens Live.”
Russell said that one day, after a “heavy dose of fight training,” Rhys told her, “We’ve met before.”
She responded, “No, we haven’t.” Rhys then reminded her about the “drunken message” he left her. “As soon as he said that, I knew exactly what he meant,” she said.
Russell said in a later interview with Variety in 2024 that they fell in love shooting the first season.
“I was in love with Matthew,” Russell said. “We were, like, hot and heavy in love, shooting the spy stuff at night in disguises and wigs. I mean, it was such a fun, sexy time. So fun, oh my gosh.”
They Kept Their Romance a Secret On Set
Rhys told Andy Cohen in a 2023 appearance on “Watch What Happens Live” that he and Russell kept their relationship private on set for “about a year.”
Rhys told People how they broke the news to their producers — not only that they were dating, but that they were expecting a baby. Their son, Sam, was born between Seasons 4 and 5.

“So when we told our producers like, ‘Oh, we do have something to say,’ they’re like, ‘Oh, don’t tell us you’re together.’ We’re like, ‘Actually, we’re going to have a baby.’ They were like, ‘Oh my God,’ because we’d kept it a secret for so long.”
Their Son, Sam, Was Born in 2016
Rhys and Russell welcomed their son, Sam, into the world in 2016. That year, Russell raved about their kid in an interview with TODAY. She said, “He’s so good. He’s big and fat and nice.”
Russell is also mom to two kids, River and Willa, from her marriage to her ex-husband, carpenter Shane Deary.
They’re Not Married — But Matthew Rhys Joked About Proposing in an Acceptance Speech

At the 2018 Emmys, Rhys won the award for outstanding lead actor in a drama series for his role in “The Americans.” When he was announced as the winner, the actor gave Russell a big kiss on before making his way to the stage.
Near the end of his acceptance speech, he peered out into the audience and thanked Russell.

“And finally, to the woman who truly got me this award, who just stands in front of me every day and just puts up with me. She said, ‘If you propose to me, I would punch you clean in the mouth.’ I don’t have the words or the time, neither which would do you justice, Keri Lynn, except thank you, more to come, thank you.”
They Were Both Nominated Multiple Times for ‘The Americans’
Keri Russell was up for an Emmy in 2016, 2017 and 2018 for “The Americans.” Rhys was nominated the same years but won in 2018.
When they were both up for Golden Globes for “The Americans” in 2019, the couple joked about their coordinated awards in an interview with with Ryan Seacrest for E! News.
“Thank God we don’t have to break up,” Russell joked.
They Recently Reunited on Screen for ‘Cocaine Bear’
In 2018, “The Americans” aired its final episode. They reunited on screen for the 2023 flick “Cocaine Bear.”

“I unashamedly jumped on my partner’s coattails because I knew (Keri Russell) was doing this movie with (director) Elizabeth Banks, who we know, and I read the script and I simply said, ‘Who’s playing that? That little fun part, a few seconds in the beginning?’ She goes, ‘I don’t know.’ I said, ‘Ask Banks.’ And then she said, ‘No, it’s been cast,’ and I said ‘Tell Banks I’ll do it.’ And then I was like, ‘Well actually, just ask her if I can do it,’” Rhys told The A.V. Club.
Rhys Supports Russell in Her ‘Diplomat’ Era
Rhys and Russell walked the red carpet together at the 2024 Golden Globes. That year, Russell was nominated for an Emmy for the Netflix drama “The Diplomat.” She’s up for an award again this year.
In an interview with Variety about her work in “The Diplomat,” Rhys gave an assessment of his partner’s personality.

“She is naturally a very shy person, and to expose herself in that way day after day, I think she finds both taxing and challenging. But she is a mind, and she loves being challenged, and she loves words — books are her biggest passion. Words and narrative are her great love.”

title: It’s the Great Pumpkin (Spice Latte), Charlie Brown: Starbucks Launches Peanuts Collection
summary: This pumpkin spice season, Starbucks is rolling out the limited-edition Peanuts + Starbucks collection items featuring a Snoopy glass cold cup.
story: The Peanuts gang is celebrating the arrival of the Great Pumpkin ... Spice Latte.

Starbucks is marking the return of everything pumpkin spice this fall by rolling out 10 collectible items featuring Snoopy, Charlie Brown and company as part of its limited-edition Peanuts + Starbucks collection.

Starbucks locations around the world will be selling the collectibles while supplies last. The collection coincides with the 60th anniversary of the classic, Halloween-themed Peanuts show “It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown.”

The headliner is a Snoopy glass cold cup with the iconic “Peanuts” character wearing a winter hat and orange beanie with his pal Woodstock perched on the top of the straw. The Snoopy glass follows the viral Starbucks Bearista cup, which caused a frenzy in 2025, was dressed up for the World Cup in July and turned pink in a separate promotion.
Here’s what to know about the Peanuts + Starbucks collection, as well as the two limited-edition, Peanuts-themed beverages that Starbucks is selling.

title: All 13 of Mariska Hargitay’s Emmys Looks — Including 1 That Honors Mom Jayne Mansfield
summary: Take a look at all of the outfits Mariska Hargitay wore as she hosted the Emmy Awards.
story: When someone says Mariska Hargitay is the hostess with the mostest, they may be referring to the number of outfits she wore.

The “Law & Order: SVU” star hosted the Emmy Awards for the first time on Sept. 14 and proceeded to wear at least 13 different outfits during the evening — and that doesn’t include what she sported in her pre-taped sketch with Taylor Swift.

Hargitay first walked the red carpet in a flowing red sequined gown with one strap hanging off her shoulder. It matched a red sparkly dress worn by her daughter, Amaya, 15, for the occasion. The Emmys carpet was a true family affair for Hargitay, who was also joined by husband Peter Hermann and their sons August, 20, and Andrew, 14.

Many fans pointed out that Hargitay and Amaya’s red dresses seemingly re-created a red dress the Emmy host’s mother, Jayne Mansfield, wore in the 1956 musical, “The Girl Can’t Help It.” Before her hosting gig, Hargitay won two Emmys for her HBO documentary “My Mom Jayne.”
But Hargitay latest homage to her mom’s fashion was merely the beginning of her cavalcade of costumes, as she slipped into a shimmering, strapless off-white dress to deliver her opening monologue.

To open the show, she joked about the audience being full of former “SVU” guest stars, celebrated her status as the first female host in 15 years, and re-created Nicole Kidman’s famous AMC ad to honor TV storytelling.
Throughout the night, Hargitay made frequent costume changes, including a sleek black gown with matching gloves, a satin white suit and a fur-lined cape paired with a sword.
Take a look at some of Hargitay’s fashion highlights worn over the course of the evening:
As the evening wound down, Hargitay said she enjoyed the experience.
“It’s been an absolute delight to be your host,” she said as the show drew to a close. “Thank you for all the love and joy tonight.
“And now that we’ve reached the end, there’s only one thing left to do,” she said as the iconic “dun, dun” from “Law & Order: SVU” played.
“God, I love it when it does that!”

title: Yes, Witney Carson Is Pregnant. And Yes, She Will Still Be Competing on ‘DWTS’: ‘It’s a Big Blessing to Do Both’
summary: On Aug. 17, “Dancing With the Stars” announced that pro dancer Witney Carson would be paired with Guillermo Rodriguez for Season 35.
story: On Aug. 17, “Dancing With the Stars” announced that pro dancer Witney Carson would be paired with Guillermo Rodriguez for Season 35. That same day, she revealed she was pregnant with her third child.

The announcement had many people wondering how she would be able to compete since the new season didn’t start for another month. But as Carson tells TODAY.com, she and husband Carson McAllister were set on expanding their family, and she didn’t think she needed to put her career on hold.

“We decided we wanted to grow our family. It’s time,” Carson, mom to sons Kevin, 5, and Jet, 3, says. “We know that we want a lot of kids and we thought it was a perfect year to start doing that. Then this opportunity came up again to do the show, and it just felt like, ‘You know what? I kind of want to prove to myself that I can do both!’ And I love both.”

Dancing since she was a child, Carson first gained fame after competing on Season 9 of “So You Think You Can Dance” in 2012.  The following year, she joined the “DWTS” troupe, before being promoted to a pro for Season 18 in 2014.

“I love to dance, and I love to compete, and I want to grow my family, as well,” the 32-year-old says. “I don’t feel like people necessarily have to lose parts of themselves to keep growing their family. That’s kind of my mantra. I’m gonna stay true to what I love and continue on my career and continue to grow my family. It’s a big blessing to be able to do both.”
For now, Carson is “feeling good,” listening to her body and making sure her baby’s healthy.

“As much as I want to dance and want to do all of it, I really have to be careful to make sure that I don’t overdo it,” she notes. “It’s perfectly safe to do all the things and I’m really not taking this any differently than I would any other season as far as mentally and physically.”

Taking it week by week, among her priorities is making sure she and her growing family are properly fueled. With a jam-packed schedule full of rehearsals and taking care of her boys with another on the way, Carson says she’s grateful for her Campbell’s partnership and the ability to make easy meals for her family.
“I remember my mom always making a hot meal with Campbell’s and so it’s very nostalgic for me,” she says. “It goes back to my childhood.”

Season 35 of “DWTS” kicks off on Sept. 15, which coincides with Campbell’s Two-Step Tuesdays launch celebrating its new sauces. Carson notes that after making a meal with the lemon garlic option, “Everyone gobbled it up ... I love to make dinner. I love doing that for my family. But I don’t have a lot of time, so being able to do something really simple like this two-step dinner is just an absolute dream.”
What is taking more than just two steps is preparing for her and Rodriguez’s competition debut. During the first episode, the duo will perform a cha cha to “Mr. Big Stuff” by Jean Knight.

“I’m really just having fun and Guillermo’s obviously very funny, he’s very heartwarming, he’s adorable,” she says of the “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” star. “He’s already so loved, and honestly, I’m really taking this season no differently than I would any other season. And I think people are a little surprised that you can continue to dance the way that I have.”

Last season, Carson took home her second Mirrorball trophy after coming in first place with Robert Irwin. While many might underestimate her and the comedian’s chances, she could go far depending on votes. (Let’s not forget how Andy Richter was dubbed “the People’s Princess” and made it to the quarterfinals.)

“There’s a TikTok floating around that’s ... not of me, but it’s of a pregnant woman and she’s got a big belly, and she’s break dancing on it,” Carson says. “And the meme is like, ‘Witney, when she makes it to the finale,’ and I’m like, ‘Oh my gosh, literally!’”
With the possibility of her baby being crowned the youngest “DWTS” champ, Carson is ready for this new adventure.
“Listen, I’m prepared for it, kind of,” she says with a laugh. “I’ve never danced this far pregnant ... But listen, I will make it happen. I mean, I’m not injured. I’m just pregnant.”

title: Emily St. John Mandel’s ‘Exit Party’ Envisions Hope in a U.S. Torn Apart by Civil War. Read the First Page
summary: Read the first page of Emily St. John Mandel’s new novel “Exit Party.” The author breaks down the book’s setting and themes.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.
Emily St. John Mandel has always been interested in the aftermath of catastrophe.
The acclaimed author of “Station Eleven” doesn’t waste any time getting to that cataclysm on the opening page of her new novel, “Exit Party,” which hits stores on Sept. 15.
“In the first spring after the collapse of the United States, the blossoming of the jacaranda trees felt to Ari like grace."
Mandel tells TODAY.com she wanted the novel’s very first line to have a “shock effect.”

“I just wanted to avoid confusion and plunge the reader immediately into this world I was creating,” Mandel tells TODAY.com. “It’s a very fast opening. We have the U.S. coming undone in literally the first sentence.”

It’s a theme Mandel has long explored in her work. In her 2014 bestseller “Station Eleven,” a group of survivors try to preserve art and human connection after the world is devastated by a deadly pandemic.
In “Exit Party,” a pair of connected storylines depict an “A side” of America splintered by civil war and a “B side” of a U.S. completely under totalitarian rule.

“I first started writing in the spring of 2022, and it seemed clear to me that I was extrapolating from our current world on the A side, where division turns into conflict,” Mandel says. “But by the time I finished the book about a year ago, I felt like I was struggling to stay ahead of the news cycle on the B side, the authoritarian state. The idea of America where secret police pick people off the street and disappear them felt fictional in 2022.”

“Exit Party” imagines how humans will try to retain connection and resilience in extreme circumstances, whether by throwing parties, putting on plays or performing a concert in a time of war or repression. Mandel says she was inspired by a 2016 story during the civil war in Syria in which residents in the war-torn town of Daraya assembled a secret underground library.
“You just want the characters to find these moments of brightness and ways to feel like you’re doing more than just surviving,” Mandel says.

The novel involves the ongoing journey of Aria, a character from her 2009 novel “The Singer’s Gun,” who has been released after 18 years in prison to an America divided by warring factions in the year 2031. She wanders a fractured Los Angeles, where the fighting has subsided for now.

“I think it’s important to me to try to kind of lean into these times when even though everything is wrong, there are moments that are good,” Mandel says. “This feeling of desperate joy at the end of the world.”
A primary theme of the novel is impermanence. A catastrophe has happened, but the characters work to find their way through to the other side of it.

“This idea that nothing lasts forever, and something always comes next after terrible moments we live through,” Mandel says. “It’s a book about resilience. Can you be resilient in these objectively awful times, because nothing lasts forever. Can you find hope in a state of impermanence?”

For those who enjoyed the Emmy-nominated “Station Eleven” television series in 2021-2022 on HBO Max, “Exit Party” is also being made for television. The feature project was bought by Laika Studios and will be produced by Amy Hodge of Fruit Tree, a film and television production company co-founded by Oscar winner Emma Stone and her husband, Dave McCary.
This time, Mandel, who did not work on the TV adaptation of “Station Eleven,” is adapting “Exit Party” for the screen.

“It’s been a challenge and fun,” she says. “I’ve always enjoyed revision, and for me, adaptation almost feels like a continuation of that. You realize pretty early on that you have to be willing to blow up the book to make it work onscreen.”
Read the First Page of Emily St. John Mandel’s ‘Exit Party’

In the first spring after the collapse of the United States, the blossoming of the jacaranda trees felt to Ari like grace. The trees bloomed in the same week that international peacekeeping troops withdrew from Los Angeles, and the convergence of flowers with the absence of foreign soldiers brought a delirious kind of hope. Everyone in the spring of 2031 knew the city was one terrorist attack away from disaster, but that peril made the season more vivid, not less.

It was Ari’s first spring outside of prison in nearly two decades, and she spent hours at a time walking the streets. Prison is a wasteland of sensory deprivation, and now the city was overwhelming. She kept expecting that the details of the world would cease to be extraordinary, but that kept not happening. No one around her seemed to notice the jacarandas, because in Los Angeles there are flowers every month of the year, but she walked streets where the trees were lit up by purple-blue blossoms and thought, My god. This place. She was forty-eight years old but felt younger, because so much of the world was new.

The United States had come undone following a coup d’état. Several states had seceded within a week of the coup, either alone or in alliances with neighbors, and war had broken out within the month. Now the fighting had subsided, for the most part, and Ari had been released into an uneasy aftermath.

title: Catherine O’Hara and Rob Reiner Receive Moving Tributes During 2026 Emmys ‘In Memoriam’
summary: Catherine O’Hara and Rob Reiner received tributes at the 2026 Emmy Awards’ “In Memoriam” segment led by performers who were close to each of them.
story: Catherine O’Hara and Rob Reiner received tributes at the 2026 Emmy Awards’ “In Memoriam” segment led by performers who were close to each of them.

O’Hara’s former co-stars — Macaulay Culkin of “Home Alone” and Annie Murphy and Dan Levy of “Schitt’s Creek — celebrated the late actor in an emotional moment that began the segment. To start, Culkin, who as a child actor played O’Hara’s character’s son in the movie franchise, described the special connection the two shared.
Follow live coverage of the 2026 Emmys

“She was encouraging. She was warm. She was funny, but the word that I think of is ‘mama.’ You know, she wasn’t just a wife and mother to Beau and Matthew. She was my mom. She was our mom, and by extension, she’s all of her mom,” Culkin said.
“She may have forgotten me, twice,” Culkin said, poking fun at the movies’ plots, “but we will always remember her.”
Murphy, who with Levy played the adult kids of O’Hara’s character in “Schitt’s Creek,” said O’Hara’s laugh “challenged anyone who heard it to join in and be as delighted as she was.”
Levy said the most important lesson he learned from O’Hara was to “say yes” to new challenges and adventures, including the joyful creation of her quirky bewigged character Moira Rose.

“Say yes to her naming that wig,” Levy said. “Say yes to giving her space to experiment and create. It will amaze you on a daily basis, and it will change your life. Say yes to her dinner invites and her stories and her wisdom and her generosity.”

Later during the “In Memoriam” segment, Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter Noah Kahan performed Simon & Garfunkel’s hit 1970 ballad “Bridge Over Troubled Water” as viewers saw images of other beloved stars who died over the past year, including Dolly Parton, James Van Der Beek, Hayden Panettiere, Eric Dane and more.
On the red carpet before the ceremony, Kahan explained to TODAY’s Sheinelle Jones why he chose to sing “Bridge Over Troubled Water” for Parton and others.
“It’s always represented so much hope and peace and kindness, which I think Dolly personified throughout her life and career,” said Kahan.

“We lost so many legends this year. I am really excited to get the chance to help memorialize them and to pay the respect to those who have contribute to this amazing industry and to art and culture,” added the singer.
The “In Memoriam” segment ended with a tearful Jamie Lee Curtis honoring late creator and director James Burrow and Hollywood director Rob Reiner, who she called a “cherished legend.”
Reiner got his start in television as an actor on “All in the Family” in the 1970s. Curtis described Reiner as “generous and kind and funny as hell and a friend to all.”
Last week, Reiner won a posthumous Emmy for a guest role on “The Bear,” Curtis revealed, breaking a record his father, comedy giant Carl Reiner, had held for longest time in between Emmy wins.
Reiner’s last Emmy award for acting came 48 years ago for “All in the Family.”
