title: Reba McEntire Honors Dolly Parton at 2026 Emmys With Touching Cover Performance
summary: Sally Field and Reba McEntire paid a special tribute to their late longtime friend Dolly Parton at the 2026 Emmys.
story: Sally Field and Reba McEntire paid a special tribute to their late longtime friend Dolly Parton at the 2026 Emmys.

“If there are truly angels on earth then we just lost one: Dolly Parton,” said Field, who co-starred alongside Parton, Julia Roberts, Shirley MacLaine, Olympia Dukakis and Daryl Hannah in the 1989 comedy “Steel Magnolias.”
“I adored her from day one and how could you not?” said Field. She remembered Parton, who died Aug. 25 at age 80 after a brief cancer battle, as “blisteringly funny.”
“She was genuine and humble and supportive,” Field said before acknowledging Parton’s humanitarianism had “made a profound difference” in the lives of many around the country.
“God bless you, Dolly Parton. I am not the only one on earth who will love you forever and forever,” Field said before footage of Parton appeared onscreen.
McEntire then took the stage to perform Parton’s ballad “Appalachian Memories.”
After Parton’s family announced her death, McEntire was among the first celebrities to pay tribute in an emotional Instagram post.
“There will never ever be another you,” McEntire wrote alongside a gallery of images of the longtime friends. “We will remember and cherish every memory and every note you ever played and sang.”
“She’s gonna have a blast in heaven singing all her favorite songs with all her family and friends who have gone on before her,” she added.
McEntire revealed during a “MasterClass” session on country music that she first met the Queen of Country in September 1977 backstage at the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville.
McEntire, who was scheduled to make her debut at the famed venue that night, learned the performance would be cut short because Parton, already a major star, had shown up unannounced.

“So I walked in, and they said, ‘Reba, I’m terribly sorry, but the two songs that we said you could sing, you’re only going to get to sing one. I said, ‘Why?’ And they said, ‘Well, Dolly Parton just pulled in the parking lot, and she’s going to take one of your songs.”
Rather than feel slighted, McEntire was thrilled.
“I said, ‘OK, can I meet her?!’” she recalled, laughing. “I didn’t care or anything. I just wanted to see Dolly Parton.”
McEntire also recalled seeing Parton for the first time backstage.
“She came walking in and I kind of backed up against the wall, and she had on the most beautiful black chiffon pantsuit with rhinestone butterflies on them and her beautiful hair,” McEntire said.
“I thought, ‘My gosh, that’s probably what an angel looks just like right there.”

title: Taylor Swift Attends Chiefs Season Opener Alongside Tom Cruise
summary: Find out if Taylor Swift attended the Chiefs vs Broncos game at Arrowhead Stadium on Sept. 14, 2026.
story: After a summer filled with love and celebration, Travis Kelce is switching his focus to the football field as his Kansas City Chiefs are set to take on the Denver Broncos in their opener to the 2026 NFL season.

The star tight end and Taylor Swift tied the knot in July at Madison Square Garden, surrounded by their family and A-list friends. Since then, Travis Kelce has been sharing a few details about the nuptials, in between discussing his hopes for the Chiefs’ season with brother Jason Kelce on their “New Heights” podcast. Now that football is officially back, the newlywed, who is entering his 14th season, is looking toward his team’s championship aspirations.
Throughout the season, he’ll likely have his bride cheering him on from the stands, where she has been frequently spotted at both home and away games since the two started dating in 2023.

The pop icon made an appearance at the season opener on Sept. 14, marking her return to Arrowhead Stadium since saying “I do”. She was photographed celebrating multiple touchdowns with Tom Cruise by her side.
Here’s what we know about the game and Swift’s attendance.
When Do the Chiefs and Broncos Play?
The Kansas City Chiefs will kick off their 2026 NFL season against the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium on Monday, Sept. 14. It will be the last game of Week 1.
What Time Do the Chiefs and Broncos Play?
The game, which will see the teams go head to head for the first time since the Broncos defeated the Chiefs on Christmas Day last year, will begin at 5:15 p.m. PT/8:15 p.m. ET.
How to Watch and Stream the Chiefs-Broncos Game?
The game will air live simultaneously on ABC and ESPN. Fans who want to stream the game can watch via Disney+.
Was Taylor Swift at the Chiefs-Broncos Game?
Yes, Swift was spotted at the Sept. 14 game between the Chiefs and Broncos. She watched the matchup with Tom Cruise. The two hugged and high-fived when the Chiefs scored.

title: Taylor Swift Appears Alongside Mariska Hargitay in Emmys ‘SVU’ Sketch
summary: Mariska Hargitay seemingly used her pull as host of the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards to get friend and longtime “Law & Order: SVU” fan Taylor Swift to appear in a sketch about the show.
story: “Saccharide. Aries. From the vineyard. North or south.”

These arbitrary phrases have left Swifties everywhere with dozens of questions after the Emmy Awards, the main one being: Is Taylor Swift the mastermind her fans know her to be, or did she just send them on a wild goose chase?

Clues point to the former. But first, let’s rewind for those who need it: Mariska Hargitay had hosted the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards on Sept. 14 and had tapped Swift, her friend and longtime “Law & Order: SVU” fan, to appear in an “SVU” parody skit that aired during the telecast.
The pre-taped sketch features Hargitay, Ice-T, Kelli Giddish, Peter Scanavino and more actors playing their characters from the crime drama. Their case to crack: Will Taylor Swift attend the Emmys?

Hargitay, as Olivia Benson, brought up as evidence Swift’s love of Easter eggs. She wheeled out a crime board filled with clues as each person took turns suggesting why certain nominees and shows pointed toward Swift making a surprise appearance.
Suddenly, a crime board was wheeled away to reveal Swift was standing in the precinct.
“Hey guys, this isn’t adding up,” she said while wearing a gray suit and holding a coffee mug.
Ice-T rebuffed her input. “And who asked you, rookie?” he said.
She replied, “Our perp has a clear M.O. A lot of this doesn’t fit the pattern, and I don’t think everything is a clue.”
“It is to the Swifties,” Hargitay quickly replied.
“I think what we’re going to be looking for is hiding in plain sight,” Swift replied.
She then panned and spoke directly to the camera: “Saccharide. Aries. From the vineyard. North or south.”
“What did you just say?” Hargitay asked her.
“I didn’t say anything,” Swift said with a shrug.

While the sketch wraps by cracking its case — Swift won’t be at the Emmys because she’ll be busy supporting husband Travis Kelce at the Chiefs season opener — the meaning of Swift’s spoken message is still a mystery.
Swifties of course know that nothing is ever that simple when it comes to the singer. They immediately began dissecting the skit on social media, seeing if they could decode a secret message.
What could it mean? Well, the Emmys executive producers have confirmed that the words have some type of significance because they were specifically chosen by Swift.

After the Emmys, executive producers Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzon-Clay from Jesse Collins Entertainment, and NBCUniversal live events and specials exec VP Jen Neal, spoke with reporters and explained how they pulled off the sketch.
“Taylor loved the script and she had some thoughts and we worked that in,” Collins told reporters, according to Variety.
One of Swift’s notes was to add Easter eggs, Collins revealed.
“She wanted them to be really official. And correct,” Rouzan-Clay shared.

As always, Swifties are on the case, and they might’ve already cracked it. Many shared their theories on social media that the sketch pointed to Swift releasing the long-awaited “Taylor’s Versions” from her debut and “Reputation” albums.
One Swiftie said on X that Ice-T’s “rookie” line and Aries, the first astrological sign, reference her self-titled first album.

Another zoomed in on the crime board and noticed a Post-it note that read “Is it TV?” adding more fuel to the fire. The board also had a heart similar to the one Swift used to draw on the back of her hand during the early days of her career.
Beneath the post, one X user replied, “Olivia said ‘the answer has been TV this whole time’ also.”
But others were more convinced that “Reputation (Taylor’s Version)” is on the way.

“I believe Debut TV is next but to add fuel to the Rep TV fire (no pun intended), if you go all the way back to the Karma MV in the Reputation scene Taylor wears the ram mask and the ram is the Aries zodiac animal,” one tweeted.
Over on Reddit, the speculation continued.
“I’m putting in my guess now — these are Rep vault track titles,” one suggested.
And one fan had a wild but plausible idea.
“OMG GUYS THERES TWO BOARDS!!! TWO!!” they said. “We are getting both Debut and Rep.”
Looks like we’ll have to wait for Swift’s next message to see what other tricks she has up her sleeve.

title: Tyler Perry Shares Plans for a Big Move After His 57th Birthday
summary: Tyler Perry, known for building his entertainment empire in Atlanta, says he’s planning to move to Puerto Rico in 2027.
story: Tyler Perry has long been synonymous with Atlanta, the home base of his entertainment empire, but the movie and television mogul says he is about to make a big move after turning 57 years old.
Perry spoke with TODAY special correspondent Justin Sylvester on Sept. 14 about making a change as he reevaluates his priorities.
“Yes, I am officially — you’re the first to hear this — I am officially moving to Puerto Rico,” Perry said. “No, this is real.”
Perry, who is the father of an 11-year-old son with ex Gelila Bekele, expects to relocate to the U.S. territory in 2027.
“Yep, moving to Puerto Rico at the top of the year, and I’m pulling back a whole lot,” he told Sylvester.
Sylvester asked him what prompted the change.
“Oh, getting older,” Perry, who turned 57 on Sept. 13, said. “It’s time to slow down a little bit, enjoy more time with my son, and just take it all in.”
He said spending more time with his son Aman has also helped him with issues related to his own childhood trauma.
“Having this opportunity and this moment to be a father and give him all the love that I never had has been really, really healing,” Perry said.
Perry’s relationship with his son and his childhood trauma are examined in the 2023 documentary “Maxine’s Baby: The Tyler Perry Story,” which was co-directed by Bekele.
In the film, a then-8-year-old Aman asks his father why he works so hard.

“Why do I work so hard?” Perry responds. “Because I want you to have a really good future and I want us to have a really good life. We can travel and have fun and help other people. So, don’t you think that’s a good idea?”
“You’re my hero,” Aman answers.
“Aw, you’re my hero!” Perry replied. “I love you.”
In 2020, Perry confirmed he and Bekele had split after a long term relationship but called her an “incredible mother” in a 2022 interview with AARP the Magazine.
Perry has tried to keep his son out of the limelight.

“My son’s not famous,” he told AARP the Magazine. “I want him to have as normal a life as he can. “I want him to know what it’s like to have his own name and his own life and not have the pressure of trying to live up to whatever or whoever your father was.”

Before Perry gets to his move to Puerto Rico, the man with more than two dozen feature films and 17 television shows to his name is still as hard working as ever. He spoke to Sylvester about his new movie, “Why Did I Get Married Again?” which began streaming on Netflix on Sept. 9.

It’s the third installment of a trilogy that began in 2007 about a group of friends who are now in their 50s. The film series also helped Perry reach a conclusion in his own life, as his age mirrors those of the characters.

“When I wrote the first one I thought, ‘You know, marriage might be a good idea at some point,’” Perry said. “But at this age, I’m like, ‘No, that’s not a good idea for me.’ So, no. Won’t be any marriage for me.”

title: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Season 35 Has a Unique Twist, Pro Witney Carson Breaks It Down
summary: “Dancing With the Stars” Season 35 will include an unexpected elimination twist that hasn’t been done before. What to know ahead of the premiere.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
“Dancing With the Stars” is switching things up for Season 35 — and some people, including the pros, have thoughts.
The dancing competition show kicks off with a two-night premiere starting at 8 p.m. on Tuesday, Sept. 15 and again on Wednesday, Sept. 16.

Sixteen couples, including three with previous dance experience, will step out onto the ballroom floor for their first dance of the season. However, in a move that hasn’t been done since 2018, there will be a double elimination during premiere week.
So what’s the major twist for Season 35 of “Dancing With the Stars”?

For night one, only the male celebrities will bust out their moves and perform a song from the year they were born. At the end of the Sept. 15 episode, one male star and their partner will be eliminated.

Night two will see the female celebrities show their skills on the dance floor, also dancing to the same theme. One female celebrity  will go home at the end of the Sept. 16 episode. This means two couples will be eliminated during week one.

“We haven’t done this before,” Witney Carson, Season 35 pro and reigning Mirrorball champion, tells TODAY.com. “It’s not really news to me that we change some things out. We stay to the core of what the show is, which is competing and dancing. All of that stays the same.”

The last time one male and female celebrity were eliminated during premiere week was during Season 26 when Olympic snowboarder Jamie Anderson and MLB star Johnny Damon were eliminated first. However, that season was condensed to a total of four episodes with only athletes competing.

“I think it’s very scary that there’s an elimination both nights because that usually doesn’t happen,” Carson, who is partnered with “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” personality Guillermo Rodriguez, says. “But at the same time, there’s a lot of couples and that’s just (the) competition. You have to vote people out, and I think people are going to have a really hard time doing that because every celebrity is so amazing.”

Fellow pro Mark Ballas also questioned whether the stars should be split into two groups based on gender. The dancer, who has competed in 22 “DWTS” seasons and is a three-time Mirrorball champ, also noted that he’s never experienced an elimination like this.
“I don’t think I was even on the show when that happened. This is a first,” he said on the Sept. 9 episode of the “Get Real” podcast, adding, “It’s not an even playing field, right?”
“It’s kind of like, boys over there, girls over there, one of you is going from each group. So that’s a little different,” he said, noting it adds pressure on the couples.
Carson, on her end, tells TODAY.com that she’s “trying to not let” the possibility of being eliminated after her first dance affect her her mindset.

“I think people are gonna have a tough time letting people go, and we will too,” she continued. “It’ll be horrible. The worst part of the show is letting people go. I wish we could all win. We’d all go to the finale.”
Who Is Competing on Night 1 of ‘DWTS’?
The first night will include a slew of male celebs, ranging from reality stars to actors to comedians and more.

The guys competing will be “The Bachelorette” alum Tyler Cameron, Paralympian Ezra French, singer Taylor Hanson, “Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” star Conner Leavitt, Savannah Bananas player Jackson Olson, “Jimmy Kimmel Live” star Guillermo Rodriguez, actor Harry Shum Jr. and influencer Connor Wood.
Who Is Competing on Night 2 of ‘DWTS’?
The ladies will hold the fort down for night two.

Competing are “Fresh Prince of Bel-Air” alum Tatyana Ali, celebrity chef Giada De Laurentiis, actor Jenna Dewan, Olympian Amber Glenn, “Traitors” and “Love Island UK” star Maura Higgins, “Summer House” star Ciara Miller, reality star Sarah Jane Nader and actor Julia Stiles.
How Will Voting Work for the Two-Night ‘DWTS’ Premiere?
Voting will work a little differently for the Season 35 “DWTS” premiere.
Voting for each night will be open only for the couples who are competing in their respective episode: male celebrities on Tuesday and female celebrities on Wednesday, according to ABC.

Viewers will have the chance to cast their vote during the live simulcast of the show in the ET/CT time zones. At that time, online voting will be available to fans in any time zone in the U.S., its territories and Canada via dwtsvote.abc.com.
Additionally, fans in the U.S. also have the chance to vote via SMS/text. The couples’ numbers to text will be shared ahead of the episodes.
The live viewer votes will then be combined with scores the judges — Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough — give to determine who is eliminated after every episode.
Witney Carson Reminds Fans That Voting Is Essential
Since the couples only get one chance before they are at risk of being eliminated, Carson says voting is vital.

“It’s not enough time. If I had it my way, I would let everyone go through to the next week,” she says. “But there’s only so many weeks that we have. It’s tough (and) it just goes to show, you have to vote!”
“You have to vote for your favorites,” she continues. “People don’t realize the votes are really, really important. If you don’t vote, then they won’t stick around.”

title: What Time Are the Emmys? How to Watch the 2026 Awards Show
summary: The 78th Emmy Awards will see some of the biggest Hollywood stars going head to head in the major categories.
story: The 78th Emmy Awards will see some of the biggest Hollywood stars going head to head in the major categories.

The 2026 Emmy Awards, television’s biggest night, will be held on Monday, Sept. 14, in Los Angeles. The ceremony will be broadcast live from Peacock Theater and feature nominees like Zendaya, Oscar Isaac, Steve Carell, Colman Domingo and more.

Mariska Hargitay, who’s cemented her icon status for her portrayal of the beloved “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” protagonist Olivia Benson, will be hosting the ceremony.  It marks the first time a woman has hosted the awards show since Jane Lynch in 2011.
Hargitay herself has already won two Creative Arts Emmys on Sept. 5 for her deeply-personal film “My Mom Jayne,” about her mother, screen legend Jayne Mansfield.
Nominations were first revealed on July 8, with TODAY exclusively sharing the nominees for outstanding variety series and outstanding reality competition program.

After all the categories were announced, “The Pitt” led with a staggering 25 nominations. “Hacks” closely followed with 24 nods for its fifth and final season, which set a record in the comedy category. Rounding out the top three was new series “Widow’s Bay” with 19 nominations.
There were also 28 actors who received their first-ever Emmy nominations. Some of them have already added “Emmy winner” to their resume, after taking home an award at the Creative Arts Emmys.
Soon, more stars will be presented with the coveted golden statue.
Read on to learn everything you need to know about the 2026 Emmys.
When Are the 2026 Emmys?
The 2026 Emmys are set to air live on Monday, Sept. 14, beginning at 5 p.m. PT/ 8 p.m. ET.
The ceremony will be held at Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.
How to Watch and Stream the 2026 Emmys
The show will be broadcast from coast-to-coast on NBC and will stream live and on demand on Peacock, as well.
Nights one and two from the Creative Arts Emmys will air on FXX on Saturday, Sept. 12, at 8 p.m. ET/PT. It will be available to stream on Hulu the following day.
Who Is Hosting the 2026 Emmys?
The Television Academy announced in July that Mariska Hargitay will emcee the event.

Hargitay has already won two Emmys for her film “My Mom Jayne,” taking home outstanding documentary and outstanding directing for a documentary/nonfiction program. The accolades make her a three-time Emmy winner.
Speaking about the honor during an appearance on TODAY in August, Hargitay shared that it took her a minute to process that she was being asked to host the major award show.

“Which is where I kind of am in my life,” the “Law & Order: SVU” star continued. “I was so incredibly honored and, again, knowing that it’s the first woman in 15 years was absolutely thrilling. And I am somebody to take on new challenges.”

title: Mariska Hargitay and Peter Hermann’s Love Story, In Their Own Words
summary: Mariska Hargitay and Peter Hermann met on the set of “Law & Order: SVU” and have been married for 22 years. Ahead of the Emmys, here’s what to know about their relationship.
story: Mariska Hargitay and Peter Hermann first met on the set of “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.” Now, 22 years of marriage later, they are going as strong as ever.

Hargitay has had a big year. Her directorial debut, the documentary “My Mom Jayne” is up for an Emmy Award and she’s set to make her hosting debut as emcee of the Sept. 14 ceremony. She also made her Broadway debut in “Every Brilliant Thing.” Her final show on July 5 was a true family affair, with Hermann appearing on stage to propose to his wife’s character.
Hargitay and Hermann started dating shortly after their initial encounter in the early 2000s, and in 2004, they got married. They’ve since welcomed three kids: August, Amaya and Andrew.
In a March 2018 interview with People, Hargitay opened up about the life that she’s created with Hermann.
“My husband is my North Star, and my kids are my teachers,” she said.
“Our family is so perfect, or at least perfect for me,” Hargitay added. “Together we’re just this whole, happy, joyful, chaotic, crazy unit. I’ve never known anything that was more right.”
Here’s a timeline of Hargitay and Hermann’s relationship, and what they have said about each other and their family in interviews.
They Met on ‘Law & Order: SVU’ in 2001

Hargitay and Hermann met in November 2001, per InStyle, when he guest-starred on Season 3 of “Law & Order: SVU.” Hargitay plays Olivia Benson, now captain of the Manhattan Special Victims Unit, and Hermann played defense attorney Trevor Langan. Since then, he’s appeared in other episodes of the 27-season show.
During a January 2022 appearance on “The Drew Barrymore Show,” Hargitay recalled their first encounter and said that she was “nervous” to be around him because he was so “handsome.”
“It was distracting,” she said.
Hargitay noted that her first thought after meeting Hermann was, “Who is that Clark Gable Superman guy that I need to marry today?”

Hargitay laughed about how her friends kept telling her that she should put herself out there more because no one was just going to show up on “Law & Order: SVU” and marry her. To their surprise, and to hers, that’s exactly what happened.
Their First Date Was at Church
Months after meeting on “Law & Order: SVU,” Hargitay said that she and Hermann were having a discussion about religion, per InStyle. She said Hermann then asked her to go to church.
Faith is important to both Hargitay and Hermann.
“I think God is very much in us. Faith is a huge part of our life. And I think everything happens for a reason,” Hargitay told SF Gate.
During the sermon, Hargitay told TODAY she got emotional — not because of the church environment, but because of their connection.

“I cried because I was feeling something that I’d never felt before, but I kind of knew what it was and I always say people, well, you know, when you’re a little girl, your parents and your grandparents and everyone goes, ‘When you’re in love, you’ll know.’ And I did,” she said. “And before I did I’d never felt that. And so when I was sitting in church, it was so hilarious, because Peter was like, ‘Oh my God, she’s so moved.’”
They Got Married in 2004
In August 2004, Hargitay and Hermann got married in Santa Barbara, California, in front of 200 guests, per People.

“I think we both knew, sort of, what we found,” Hargitay later told People in 2019. “We sort of knew that we found the right one. I never thought it could be this good, and I never knew that I’d be reminded on the journey, that I’d marry the right one. That I waited and married the right one and it’s better than I thought it was. Because sometimes you take a snapshot and you go, ‘I can’t believe this is my life.’”
They Welcomed Son August in 2006
In June 2006, Hargitay and Hermann welcomed their first child, son August Miklos Friedrich Hermann.

“Nobody wanted to be pregnant more than me,” the “Lake Placid” star told SELF magazine in 2007. “From the minute I found out, I was wearing full-on maternity pants. My stomach was totally flat, mind you, but I was just so excited.”
In a 2019 interview with Traveling Mom, Hargitay said having a child made her and Hermann more “compassionate toward other people.”

“You go from being that person who would get annoyed at the sound of a crying baby, hoping it would just go to sleep, to the one who is completely empathic toward the parents, hoping the baby is OK and wondering if there is anything you can do to help,” she said. “Now, we’re all in the same boat. We’re on the same team, which is one of my favorite things about becoming a parent. I feel like I’m in the club now.”
They Adopted Daughter Amaya in April 2011
In April 2011, Hargitay and her hubby adopted daughter Amaya Josephine Hermann.

“I’m deliriously happy,” Hargitay told People at the time. “From the minute she was born, she was just surprisingly alert and so full of love.” According to People, the couple’s daughter was born in the United States.
Before Hermann and Hargitay adopted her, they were “considering both international and domestic adoption” for their second kid.
“We talked a lot about mixed-race adoptions, and we are very excited that we are now a multi-racial family. We’re just so happy she’s here,” Hargitay said.
As for August? The “Tales from Earthsea” star noted that the then 4-year-old took to being an older brother easily.
“He calls her his baby because he says the whole thing was his idea,” she said. “He always talks about how he’s going to protect her. He’s going to be a great big brother.”
... And They Adopted Son Andrew Months Later
In October 2011, Hargitay and Hermann adopted their third child, son Andrew Nicolas Hargitay Hermann, just months after they became parents to Amaya.
In an interview with People, Hargitay said that she barely had any clothes to give him because she gave all of August’s old clothes to her godson, who was born a few months before Andrew.
“It was so hilarious,” she said.
But thanks to her friends, Hargitay was able to clothe her baby in a few onesies that they brought over.

While Hargitay and Hermann were considering adopting another child, Andrew’s adoption came more quickly than anticipated. In an interview with Good Housekeeping, Hargitay explained they received word of a premature child and that saying yes was a “no-brainer.”
“It was like … a miracle. And I don’t use that word lightly. I’ve never made a bigger decision so quickly,” Hargitay aid.
Once the paperwork was finalized, Hargitay told People they felt “so lucky” to be parents again.

“We never in a million years thought it would happen this quickly, but something inside of us knew that this was right, and we said, ‘Yes, yes, yes!’” she explained to People. “We knew this was our guy. Everything about it felt right. It felt divinely right.”
After taking Andrew home, Hargitay felt more joy than she could ever imagine.
“I always describe it as this angel that fell out of the sky, because he was a little unexpected,” she told People in 2019.

“It’s something that happened very quickly, when adoption can take a long time,” Hargitay added. “We were so beautifully and surprisingly … not because we’re not in sync, but surprisingly in sync about something so huge. So momentous.”
They Just Celebrated Their 22nd Anniversary
In August 2026, Hargitay and Hermann celebrated their 22-year wedding anniversary.
To commemorate the occasion, Hargitay shared a black-and-white photo of them in Cannes, France, seemingly from 2025, when she debuted “My Mom Jayne” at the city’s film festival.
“Happy 22nd anniversary Peter Hermann. You’ve got all my love,” she captioned the photo.
Mariska Hargitay Revealed How She Keeps Her Marriage So ‘New and Fresh’

Amid their 20th wedding anniversary, when asked how she keeps their marriage so “fresh,” Hargitay told Jenna Bush Hager on TODAY with Hoda & Jenna that it has everything to do with how she views their romance.

“I’m at a point in my life where it just keeps getting better with him. And marriage is not always like this,” Hargitay said, while putting her arm in an upright position, “or any relationship that is deep in matters. But, I have learned so much.”

“Peter always says this beautiful quote about ... breaking through marriage into marriage,” she continued. “And that is what I think we’ve lived because at this time in my life, I feel very different than I have for the last maybe 15 or 18 — and I feel (assured) up in our love.”
Mariska Hargitay and Peter Hermann Have Brought Their Kids to Red Carpets

While rare, Hargitay and Hermann occasionally bring their three kids to red carpets, including in May 2023, when the whole family attended the Stuttering Association for the Young Benefit Gala in New York City.
Hargitay and Hermann have been outspoken about August, now 20, and his stutter. Both actors were inducted into the Stuttering Association for the Young’s Hall of Fame.
“It’s been so exciting to learn and to understand and educate people because as soon as people know, they’re like, ‘Oh, my gosh. Thank you. Tell me more. Tell me more,’” Hargitay told People in 2023.
In 2025, Hargitay brought August, Amaya and Andrew along for several red carpet events for her film “My Mom Jayne,” including its debut at Cannes Film Festival and its New York City premiere.
Peter Hermann Proposes To Mariska Hargitay (For A Second Time)

At Hargitay’s closing night performance of “Every Brilliant Thing,”  an interactive one-person play and Hargitay’s Broadway debut, Hermann filled an audience-participant role given to someone in the crowd.
The role of Sam, the character’s childhood best friend and eventual spouse, was played by Hermann during Hargitay’s July 5 show.
Hermann got down on one knee to act out a proposal, which received lots of laughter and cheers from the audience.
Hargitay and Hermann shared an on-stage hug and a kiss to close out her Broadway run.
Peter Hermann Plays Plus One At Creative Arts Emmys Awards
Mariska Hargitay took home two trophies at the Creative Arts Emmys Awards on Sept. 5.
Peter Hermann, adorned in an all-black suit, walked the red carpet with Hargitay following the ceremony, and the two posed together with her hardware.

For her documentary “My Mom Jayne,” Hargitay won outstanding documentary or nonfiction special. From her role as director, she also secured the win for outstanding directing for a documentary/nonfiction program.

title: Our 1 Big Question for Mariska Hargitay During Commercial: How Does It Feel to Be Mariska Hargitay?
summary: Mariska Hargitay opens up about the healing she found in making “My Mom Jayne,” hosting the Emmys and how Knicks point guard, Jalen Brunson, has inspired her.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.

In Hollywood, there are A-listers and then there’s royalty. Mariska Hargitay lands in the latter category. The daughter of screen legend Jayne Mansfield, Hargitay has followed in her mother’s footsteps, becoming luminary in her own right for her portrayal of Olivia Benson on “Law & Order: SVU.”
It’s a role that’s earned her both an Emmy and a Golden Globe. Not to mention that, at 27 years and counting, it’s the longest-running primetime series in NBC history.

On this day, however, Hargitay hasn’t come to unpack the latest season of the crime drama. Instead, we sit down in TODAY’s Orange Room to talk about the latest season of her life, a chapter that’s been especially fulfilling for a number of reasons.

Among them? She’s just wrapped her successful Broadway debut, sat courtside with bestie Taylor Swift before her beloved Knicks took home the championship, and premiered the deeply personal film “My Mom Jayne,” which earned the 62-year-old yet another an Emmy nomination.

If she wins, she won’t have far to go to pick up the trophy since Hargitay is also hosting the Emmys this year, the first time a woman has hosted the awards show since Jane Lynch held the distinction back in 2011.

It’s undoubtedly Hargitay’s moment. The actor reflects on the “profound healing” that got her here and how the Knicks’ Jalen Brunson played a part in it. She also delves into her work with the Purple Leash Project, a partnership between Purina and the nonprofit RedRover that spotlights the need for more pet-friendly domestic violence shelters, an initiative near and dear to her heart.
This interview has been lighted edited for clarity.
First of all, I just want to acknowledge the fact that I didn’t think about it either and that’s what hit me so hard when I learned about it, because I don’t think anybody thinks about that.

So, it’s a really powerful and extraordinary initiative. Just the idea that a survivor shouldn’t have to choose between her safety and her animals. There’s already so many barriers of why not to leave and why not to go, but this one is a huge one.

This idea that pets are actually family members and oftentimes the most consistent, steady presence in a survivor’s life, that provides so much comfort, so much support, so much safety, really. And here was a reason that people weren’t going.

Up to 50% of survivors were not wanting to go, to leave their animals. So, it’s actually a brilliant initiative to a way of  supporting survivors. It takes that off their plate and they’re doing it all over and I was just so moved by it and so happy to get on board.

They’re like your children. They are an extended part of your family. Also, the idea of animals being used as threats or used as tactics to keep the person there or threaten that if they leave, they’ll hurt the animal. More than 70% of women in shelters report that their abuser has used an animal as a form of control.
So, it’s innovative, brilliant and so survivor-centric. And it is truly something that supports healing and gives survivors the courage to leave and supports them in a profound way.

I’ll tell you what it feels like: When I made this film, everything changed. I think the way I described it is finding so much more internal space that I didn’t have. It really settled my nervous system and was very profoundly healing for me in ways I was aware of, and in ways that I wasn’t.

My friend Kelli Giddish, my amazing co-star, had said to me after she saw (“My Mom Jayne”), because she knows me very well, she says, “I can’t wait to see what you do next,” and that really resonated with me really deeply.
For me, it wasn’t an accident that all this ... it was like a pathway started opening up because I think, and I’ve always believed, that the only way out is through. That’s sort of my motto.
This is also why I made this film, this is why I did that. Because I was carrying something that I didn’t want to carry and I realized, wasn’t mine to carry.

So, in a way, yes, I’m doing all these amazing things and I’m doing all these new things. In a way, it’s surprising and sort of unbelievable. And in a way, it feels like, “Of course. Now.” Because I’ve gotten ready for it internally.

I’ve always been a person to take on new challenges, but the fact that these opportunities are coming – I think that something shifted. So when the play came, I was 62. My mother was 22 (when she made her Broadway debut), and I made this film. So, I just believed that it wasn’t an accident that after I made the film, it sort of cleared that out and dealt with it and had a new reconciliation and new peace with it and so much new discovery.
So, the fact that the play came, I went, “Of course it did.” And I feel a little bit like that with the Emmys. As much as it was a shocker for me, I went, “Got it.”

Even Jalen (Brunson), all the Knicks stuff, that’s been so fun and exciting and he really is like my excellence mentor or my teacher of what’s possible in a very similar way that my dad was for me. I think that’s what also I love about him because my dad said, “You can do anything, you just have to set your mind to it.” That’s how I was raised.

So, when I see what Jalen has accomplished with the odds he goes up against, and his work ethic, and the fact that he holds a space to win, always, always, there’s no quitting ever with him, which is what my dad taught me.

It’s like, we don’t quit in this family. We keep going. It depends how much you want it. So it’s sort of this beautiful duality, that on one hand it’s, “Oh my gosh.” And on the other hand, it feels natural and I’m excited and ready in a way.

title: How to Watch the 2026 Emmys Red Carpet Ahead of the Ceremony
summary: Stars from some of the biggest shows of the past year are in Los Angeles to celebrate the 2026 Emmys.
story: Stars from some of the biggest shows of the past year are in Los Angeles to celebrate the 2026 Emmys.

The 78th Emmy Awards, hosted by Mariska Hargitay, will air live on NBC and stream on Peacock on Monday, Sept. 14. The Television Academy announced the star-studded list of nominees in July, and many of them are expected to make appearances.

Actors like Jason Bateman and Oscar Isaac are battling in the stacked outstanding lead actor in an anthology series or movie category, which includes Riz Ahmed, Charlie Hunnam and Matthew Rhys, too. Meanwhile, Zendaya is trying to pick up her third Emmy win in the outstanding lead actress in a drama series category for her portrayal of Rue in “Euphoria.” But, she faces tough competition from fellow nominees Carrie Coon, Keri Russell, Rhea Seehorn and Chase Infiniti.
While television fans are waiting to find out who will snag the trophy, they are also looking forward to seeing what the actors will be wearing when they make their grand arrivals at Peacock Theater.

And it’s not just the nominees who will be dressed to the nines. Previously announced presenters like Sarah Michelle Gellar, Keke Palmer, Florence Pugh, Marcello Hernández and more will be in attendance as well to hand out awards throughout the night.
Make sure you don’t miss a moment of the show, including the arrivals during the pre-shows. Find out how to watch all the red carpet arrivals below.
When Are the 2026 Emmys?
The 78th Emmy Awards will be broadcast live from coast—to—coast on NBC on Monday, Sept. 14. The show will also be available to stream live and on demand on Peacock.
The ceremony begins at 5 p.m. PT/ 8 p.m. ET.
How to Watch the 2026 Emmys Pre-Shows
There will be plenty of pre-shows that fans can tune into to catch all the major moments from television’s biggest night.

E! will air its “Live From E!: Countdown to The Emmys” special starting at 2 p.m. PT/ 5 p.m. ET. The pre-show will last for one hour and will be hosted by Erin Lim Rhodes, along with Lance Bass and Ciara Miller.
Then, Justin Sylvester, Keltie Knight and Will Marfuggi will step in to lead “Live From E!: 2026 Emmys” for two hours before the show begins, starting at 3 p.m. PT/ 6 p.m. ET.

Those who prefer streaming to cable can check out People and Entertainment Weekly’s websites. Throughout the day, both outlets will be posting red carpet interviews on their sites and respective social media platforms.
NBC will also be active on social media, with a pre-show TikTok live from the red carpet. The livestream will kick off at 4:45 p.m. PT/ 6:35 p.m. ET on tiktok.com/@nbc.

Another pre-show option for Los Angeles locals is KTLA’s “Live From The Emmys” rundown. Newscasters Jessica Holmes and Melvin Robert will share details with viewers live from the red carpet from 3 p.m to 5 p.m. PT. Journalist Megan Henderson and Doug Kolk will also be on hand to report.

Finally, CNN and Variety are teaming up to bring fans joint coverage. “CNN & Variety: Red Carpet Live: TV’s Biggest Night” will be available on CNN’s website and on the CNN app for subscribers at 2 p.m. PT/ 5 p.m. ET. CNN reporter Elizabeth Wagmeister and Variety’s co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh will work together for the coverage.
How to Watch the 2026 Emmys Backstage Feed
Once the show officially begins, Emmys.com and youtube.com/@televisionacad will stream footage live from a backstage feed.

The behind-the-scenes videos will include moments from the Thank You Cam, Backstage Cam, Emmy Photo Lounge and Winnerviews, which will be hosted by Albert Lawrence. Fans can also check out additional clips from the red carpet, show and press room.

title: From ‘Traitors’ to ‘Dancing With the Stars,’ Mark Ballas Had to Learn to Trust Partner Maura Higgins
summary: Mark Ballas shares with TODAY.com his experience competing on “Traitors” with his now-“Dancing With the Stars” partner Maura Higgins.
story: Mark Ballas’ main goal when competing on “Dancing With The Stars” is always for his celebrity partner to “enjoy the experience and try our best.”
But when he found out that for Season 35, he would be partnered with his former “The Traitors” co-star Maura Higgins, he had to adjust a bit and learn how to trust her.

“‘The Traitors’ is a wild psychological experience,” the 40-year-old professional dancer and three-time Mirrorball champion tells TODAY.com. “And we made it to the last episode together. She made it further than me, obviously, to the last two (people). I think I made it to the last six or last five.”

Season 35 of “DWTS” will kick off with a two-night premiere on Sept. 15 and Sept. 16. During the first episode, only the male celebrities will perform, while Ballas and Higgins will get to show off their skills on the second night when only the female celebrities get to compete.
Previously, the two appeared on the fourth season of “Traitors,” the hit Peacock competition series, which is famously known for its backstabbing and deceitful game play among contestants.

While the pair were both “Faithfuls,” contestants spend the duration of the season, unsure of whether they can trust their fellow players who may just be “Traitors” in disguise who will “murder” — aka eliminate — them.

“We got along, but at the same time we couldn’t fully trust each other because, I mean, there was a moment where I was convinced it was her and Rob (Rausch),” Ballas says, referencing his fellow competitors. “So much stuff didn’t make the edit on ‘The Traitors.’ (We had) so many conversations. However, we did have a laugh together ... But you can’t trust each other in there. You’d be stupid to.”

The two, however, did bond during their time on “Traitors,” dishing on their European ties. Higgins is Irish and Ballas grew up in England with a Texan father and a British mother, both of whom were ballroom dancers.
He recalls Higgins, who also starred in “Love Island UK,” telling him while in the Scottish castle that she would love to compete on “Dancing With the Stars.”

“I was like, “Girl, you can’t make it through a 45-minute challenge. You ain’t making it through ‘Dancing With the Stars,’” he jokes. “But she was like, ‘No, it’s different. I want to dance. I want to learn how to dance. I don’t want to carry gold pebbles in a backpack up a mountain.’”
After their “Traitors” experience, they saw each other at the reunion. Higgins also attended his “Chicago The Musical” show on Broadway.
But when he found out she was his partner, he thought, “‘This is hilarious,’ because she manifested this, right? I’m a big believer in manifestation.”
While Higgins has never had any dance training, he says “she’s a hard worker.”

“To my surprise, after seeing her in the challenges on ‘The Traitors,’ I’ve been impressed with how she’s putting a chin down and getting into it,” he says. “But she is a true beginner, which is exciting. I’m excited about that challenge. And we have to also establish real trust and friendship because in ‘The Traitors,’ unless you play that game, I can’t explain what it does to you mentally. It’s wild.”
For their competition debut, the pair will perform a foxtrot to “Black Velvet” by Alannah Myles. In preparation, Ballas has been making sure the reality star is diving into the experience.
Ballas’ No. 1 tip for aspiring dancers, regardless of experience? Don’t hold back.
“Take the dive off the diving board. Don’t be afraid,” he says. “If you’re signing up for something like this, really make sure you want to do it. And if you’re here, try your best.”

He hopes all his partners have felt like they’ve gotten the best experience they possibly could have with no regrets. As for Higgins, he calls her a “great personality” and has helped her loosen up by having her poke fun at him.

“I’m a very full-out, expressive person as it is. So when we’re learning moves, I’ll demonstrate a move and I’ll do it almost over the top, silly,” he shares. Then he will ask his partner to re-create the move “and nine times out of 10 when they do that, they nail it.”
In Higgins’ case, he says, “I was like, ‘Can you just make fun of me for a minute?’ And she made fun of me, did the face and threw her arms and I was like, ‘Yes, like that!’”
For now, he stresses that this is a once in a lifetime experience for the celebrities, encouraging them to really take it in.

“Think about it, it’s quite silly. Like, we’re ballroom dancing on telly and you get a new style every six days, and you’re just hoping that you make it to the end,” he says. “For me the mission is, every week just a bit better, as long as we last.”

title: Celebrities Turned The U.S. Open Into A Masterclass On Style
summary: The tournament, which concluded on Sept. 13 with Alexander Zverev besting Ben Shelton in the men’s singles finals, also featured some impressive style from celebrities.
story: Fans may have attended the U.S. Open for the exceptional tennis, but they got a serving of great style on the side.

The tournament, which concluded on Sept. 13 with Alexander Zverev besting Ben Shelton in the men’s singles finals, has become one of the biggest events in sports, boasting star-studded crowds and a whole lot of excitement at the Arthur Ashe Stadium in Queens, New York. And celebrities have matched the energy with some truly exquisite looks.
From star athletes to actors, check out the many celebrities who brought some striking looks to one of the most buzzy sporting events of the year.
Paris Hilton

If there’s one thing reality star Paris Hilton is going to do, it’s stun. Hilton hit the Blue Carpet in pieces from Thom Browne and Gucci. She paired her sweater top and skirt with an adorable pink dog purse for the occasion.
Eiza González
Actor Eiza González went for a chic monochrome off-white look with a high-neck, sleeveless bodysuit and trousers.
Maitreyi Ramakrishnan
Actor Maitreyi Ramakrishnan hit the Blue Carpet with a flowing, patterned summer dress and open-toed black heels.
Spike Lee and Tonya Lewis
In true Spike Lee fashion, the director attended the tournament, repping the New York Yankees. His wife Tonya Lewis Lee sported a classic brown suit, paired with pointed-toe heels.
Alysa Liu
Figure Skater and Olympian Alysa Liu pulled up to the U.S. Open in her signature tomboy style with a camo-colored jacket and pants, paired with a plain white tee.
Pink and Jameson Moon Hart

Singer Pink coordinated her U.S. Open look with her son, Jameson Moon. The singer wore a green jacket with a white shirt-and-pants combo underneath, while Jameson rocked a green-and-white striped fit.
Jordyn Woods
Model Jordan Woods went with a denim ensemble, completing the look with a chic brown bag and, of course. The newlywed also flashed her gorgeous emerald-cut diamond ring.
Trinity Rodman

Soccer star Trinity Rodman, whose boyfriend Ben Shelton is playing in the men’s singles finals, brought many standout looks to the Open. But one highlight was this plaid zip-up jacket and skirt combo, completed with a bright orange cap.
Morena Baccarin and Ben McKenzie
Actor Morena Baccarin hit the Blue Carpet with an orange leather dress while her hubby and fellow actor Ben McKenzie wore a classic button-down and maroon trousers.
Ashlyn Harris and Sophia Bush

Former pro soccer player and two-time World Cup champ Ashlyn Harris wore a long-sleeved white button down and pin-striped trousers to the Open. Meanwhile, her girlfriend actor Sophia Bush  sported a green jacket, paired with a white dress and shoes that flaunted mis-matched colors.
Daniela Rajic and Paul George

Boston Celtics’ Paul George dressed up a Brown Ralph Lauren shirt with a flashy cross necklace. His wife and entrepreneur Daniela Rajic went for a black halter top and white pants, paired with a black mini-purse.
Savannah Guthrie and Michael Feldman

TODAY’s Savannah Guthrie hit the Blue Carpet, wearing a long floral, striped skirt, a plain black top and a heart-shaped necklace. Her husband Michael Feldman sported a classic blue suit and dressy sneakers.
Olivia Palermo
Influencer and fashionista Olivia Palermo rolled up to the U.S. Open in a polka-dotted dress paired with pink flats that had red accents on top.
Natalia Bryant
Model Natalia Bryant, daughter of the late basketball great Kobe Bryant, attended the tournament wearing an off-the-shoulder button down dress. She opted to pair the outfit with a pair of flip-flops.
Trae Young
Washington Wizards’ Trae Young went for a sporty look, with an off-white button down shirt to match his shorts.
Landry Shamet and Cameron Aimonetti

New York Knicks’ Landry Shamet brought some color to the Blue Carpet with a patterned sweater and burgundy hat. His camera strapped around his neck added an extra touch. His fiance Cameron Aimonetti sported a classic white button-down and jeans.
Aziz Ansari
While comedian Aziz Ansari kept his look classic with a striped blue button-down and khaki pants, he added just a bit of spark with a pair of oversized shades.
Ali Marks and Jalen Brunson

New York Knicks captain Jalen Brunson arrived at the U.S. Open, wearing a khaki jacket paired with a plain white tee. His wife, Ali Marks, sported a floral sleeveless dress and a red sweater, wrapped around her shoulders.
Tommy Hilfiger and Dee Ocleppo Hilfiger

Designers Tommy Hilfiger and Dee Ocleppo Hilfiger showed up to the match sporting the classic Hilfiger red, white and blue colors. Dee Ocleppo Hilfiger wore a plaid jacket while Tommy Hilfiger opted for a classic suit and sweater.

title: Hayden Panettiere’s Ex Brian Hickerson And His Brother Involved In A Bar Altercation, Police Say
summary: Brian Hickerson, Hayden Panettiere’s on-again-off-again boyfriend, was recently involved in an altercation at a bar in South Carolina, police say.
story: Brian Hickerson, Hayden Panettiere’s on-again-off-again boyfriend, was recently involved in an altercation at a bar in South Carolina, police say.

The Greenville Police Department identified Brian Hickerson and his brother Zachary Hickerson as two individuals involved in the incident at Wild Wing Cafe on Sept. 12, law enforcement told NBC News in a statement.
Zachary Hickerson, who was “highly intoxicated,” was taken into custody and charged with disorderly conduct while Brian Hickerson was released from the scene, police said.
The incident comes just weeks after a police report showed that the brothers were present when Panettiere was pronounced dead on Aug. 18.
Zachary Hickerson and Brian Hickerson did not immediately respond to NBC News’ requests for comment.

According to Greenville Police, officers were dispatched to the restaurant at around 9:10 p.m. on Saturday in response to a reported assault. The officers detained multiple patrons as the situation was being investigated before determining that Zachary Hickerson had been heavily inebriated.

“He began yelling profanities in a public setting, and as a result, he was taken into custody for disorderly conduct and transported to the Greenville County Detention Center,” police said in a statement.
Brian Hickerson was not charged.

In August, EMS personnel responded to a 911 call to Panettiere unresponsive at an apartment, where the brothers also were, according to a heavily redacted police report. Panettiere was in cardiac arrest when emergency personnel arrived. A cause of death has not been released.

Zach Hickerson was “very emotional” during the resuscitative efforts on Panettiere, Greenville Officer Matthew Bryan wrote in the report. Brian Hickerson “did not become emotional until EMS declared her officially deceased,” Bryan wrote.

title: Benny Blanco Reveals The Simple Way He Won Over Selena Gomez: ‘I Didn’t Use Black Magic Or Anything’
summary: Record producer Benny Blanco seems to have cracked the code for success in many aspects of life, including romance. He joined Willie Geist for Sunday Sitdown.
story: Record producer Benny Blanco seems to have cracked the code for success in many aspects of life, including romance.
In a conversation with host Willie Geist on TODAY’s Sunday Sitdown, Blanco shared how he won over his wife, actor and singer Selena Gomez.

“Men, listen up. Okay, first of all, I gotta be the poster child for the guy you gotta listen to. Look at me,” Blanco said between laughs. “I have the most beautiful wife in the world. I did it and I didn’t use black magic or anything. I just was nice.”

Blanco expanded on his relationship philosophy and what he’s learned from Gomez, with whom he collaborated with for years on tracks like “Same Old Love” and “Single Soon.” The couple, who confirmed their relationship in 2023, tied the knot in September 2025.

“It’s understanding your partner, and being able to talk about things, and have an open dialogue,” he told Willie. “We’re in a really good spot, and I’m very fortunate. And I think, again, like, not being a d*** and being nice to people put her into my orbit at the right time.”

Blanco, who’s behind some of the biggest hits like Katy Perry’s “California Gurls,” Justin Bieber’s “Love Yourself” and Rihanna’s “Diamonds,” can add another highlight to his list of accomplishments. He spoke to Willie about his upcoming book “F*ck Failure,” which explores his mindset when it comes to turning adverse moments into achievements.

“I think a lot of people probably look at you and they’re like, ‘Huge success professionally. Great personal life. Seems happy, and charismatic, and all the things,’” Willie said. “So, what makes you an expert on failure?”
Blanco responded, describing himself as “the biggest failure in the world.”

“I’ve failed so many times,” Blanco said. “I failed yesterday. I finished a mix from one of my songs. I gave it to the artist. They didn’t like it. They wanted to redo something. And what am I gonna do, like, cry about it? No.”

Blanco said his book tells real stories about times he’s failed and how those experiences have helped him get to where he is today.  He said hopes that readers won’t have to make all the same mistakes he did.

The producer credited his family helping him build his confidence. He also said that Ed Sheeran, who he’s worked with extensively on the singer’s hit album “Divide,” gave him valuable advice about attitude.

“I was talking with Ed Sheeran, and he said, ‘Don’t give people the opportunity to not wanna help you,’” Blanco shared. “Like, if somebody asks you to do something, and it’s seems really small, just do it. It takes so much energy to be a d***.”
Blanco has previously spoken about his relationship with Gomez. In May 2024, he joined TODAY With Hoda & Jenna and shared how his cooking helped steal the heart of his his now-wife.
“F*ck Failure” will be published by Simon & Schuster on Sept. 15.

title: Our 1 Main Question for ‘Practical Magic 2’s’ Xolo Maridueña During Commercial: What’s It Like Being in the Sisterhood?
summary: Xolo Maridueña sits down to talk all things “Practical Magic 2,” including plans for a sequel and how he felt working with Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock
story: Xolo Maridueña is pretty much the nicest person ever. Warm, charming and a smile that reaches his eyes, it’s easy to see why Sandra Bullock was interested in the “Cobra Kai” actor for the Gideon, love interest of Bullock’s on-screen daughter, in “Practical Magic 2.”

If it’s been a minute since you’ve seen the original, the story revolves around Sally (Bullock) and Gillian Owens (Nicole Kidman), a pair of witch sisters and their eccentric aunts Jet (Dianne Wiest) and Franny (Stockard Channing), who grapple with an ancient death curse placed on any man they fall in love with.

The latest installment finds Sally’s two daughters Kylie (Joey King) and Antonio (Maisie Williams) all grown up and in Kylie’s case, head over heels in love. Unaware of her witchy lineage, Kylie professes her love and, you guessed it, Gideon almost instantly becomes yet another casualty of the Owens Curse. The result is a supernatural goose chase across England in hopes of saving him.

On the final stop of the “Practical Magic 2” press tour, Maridueña, sits down with TODAY.com to share his thoughts on the unique sisterhood in “Practical Magic,” the possibility of another film and how one phone call changed his life.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.
There is definitely something different when you have a woman writer, women producers, a woman director, a No. 1 on the call sheet, No. 1 through No. 5 on the call sheet, that are women as well.

There is something absolutely palpable that, especially for a story of this nature, I think fit like a glove. To your point, I guess as a male, one of the few men in this movie, I never felt “othered” in a way that I’m sure on the flip side ... movies are a male-dominated field, especially behind the camera.

To have a movie that, not only in front of the camera, is trying to tell the story about matriarchy and the power of women, to talk the talk and walk the walk, I thought was something incredible. I hope it happens more in movies that aren’t necessarily where the main pillar is not sisterhood. This should be allowed to happen everywhere.

The challenge for me, the objective was, we need a handful of scenes to not only make you believe that these two people love each other, but that this is the first person Kylie is going to say “I love you” to.

For me, all of my scenes were make it or break it, because if this relationship isn’t believable, then the whole movie you’re like, “Why is she going on this journey for this guy who’s not even all that and a bag of chips, you know?”

So, in that way, I was very blessed and really have been in my career thus far with getting to play really optimistic, joyous, uplifting characters. It’s been such a help in my own personal life to get to work through scenes with a character who has this mindset and I think “Practical Magic” is no different.

I still am having a hard time wrapping my head around it. It still feels surreal. We just finished. This, literally, this conversation is going to be the exclamation point on this “Practical Magic” journey for me.

From the very first day that I got the call that Sandy was interested in me hopping on board, it instantly feels like a moment where your whole life has been waiting for this opportunity to be let in by the greats and allowed to kind of bear witness to their process.

And that’s not even just Sandy, Nicole, that’s Stockard and Dianne, that’s Maisie and Joey. That’s Susanne (Bier), our director, Denise (Di Novi), our producers. That really goes for everyone. It lived up to all of those expectations.

Of course! I signed onto the second with the third in mind. I really ended up loving what transpired in the second one, how the end does pass the baton, but we get this family, the mother and daughter duo, for the whole movie. I’m super excited about the prospect of figuring out what the story is now.

This movie has done such a great job of being able to keep the themes and the heart of the movie without needing to keep the formula or repeat the same steps. I think if there is a third one, it’ll surely kind of continue with this in that the curse is broken now, but they still have magic. So, I think there’s other areas to explore.
I could be, like, a normal dad who has magic kids (laughs).

title: U.S. and China face grave AI risks but mutual distrust stalls cooperation
summary: The United States and China are both gripped by safety fears as they reckon with their rapid advances in AI, but intensifying competition and deep mutual distrust could derail the kind of cooperation experts say is vital to head off the strategically vital technology’s greatest dangers.
story: BEIJING — The United States and China are both gripped by safety fears as they reckon with their rapid advances in AI, but intensifying competition and deep mutual distrust could derail the kind of cooperation experts say is vital to head off the strategically vital technology’s greatest dangers.

Artificial intelligence is increasingly at the center of the rivalry between Washington and Beijing, and it is expected to be a major topic of discussion at a summit in Washington next week between President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

The summit comes as AI leaders and researchers in the U.S. warn that companies should “slow the pace” of AI development, citing recent incidents involving autonomous agents. Trump has dismissed such concerns as a “hoax” while agreeing with executives such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei that the U.S. must maintain AI dominance over China through export controls and other measures.
How exactly could AI cause widespread danger?

China, which tightly regulates AI and largely avoids the existential worries the technology provokes in the U.S., has interpreted calls to slow its development as targeted squarely at its own progress. U.S. companies say the Chinese AI sector is being driven in part by large-scale “illicit distillation” of their most advanced models.
Chinese officials, who say distillation is a conventional practice that U.S. companies also use on Chinese models, in turn accuse America’s AI executives of trying to stave off competition.
Senior Col. Zhu Qichao, a noted voice on Chinese military AI and national security, called for “cooperation” with the U.S. while warning against “vicious competition.”

“Because with the development of emerging technologies, it definitely comes with many possibilities,” said Zhu, the director of the Institute for Defense Technology and Strategic Studies at the People’s Liberation Army National University of Defense Technology.
“On one hand, it benefits humanity, but on the other hand, there are also considerations regarding risks,” he told NBC News on Tuesday at the Xiangshan Forum in Beijing.

AI and the worries around it were a major focus at the annual defense forum, where rooms were packed with scholars, military officials and commentators from the U.S. and other countries, many of which are being pressured to pick sides in the U.S.-China AI race.
Though Trump and Xi agreed at their May summit in Beijing to hold high-level AI talks, no such talks have been publicly confirmed ahead of Xi’s visit next week.
Wu Xinbo, dean of the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai, said China was wary that the talks could be used to further slow its progress.

“On the other hand, I think both sides need to sit down to talk about the risks posed by AI development,” he said at the forum, adding that “it will take a long way before the two sides can really forge some important consensus on this issue.”
For U.S.-China cooperation to work, the U.S. needs to be open to both sides benefiting, said Francesca Giovannini, executive director of the Harvard Belfer Center’s Initiative on Managing the Atom.

“The United States operates on a very specific type of theory. And the theory is, whoever wins the AI race wins everything,” she said in an interview at the forum. “So if this is your zero-sum game idea, you won’t be conceding anything.”

China is unlikely to agree to a slowdown at the behest of U.S. AI companies, said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at the Asia Group, an American strategic advisory firm based in Washington.

“I don’t think what happens in the U.S. really matters to China,” he said Tuesday in a phone interview from Hong Kong. “They want to do AI at their own pace, and to a very large degree a lot of people in the industry, in the government, they have a very proud sense that this is finally the chance for China.”

China, which sees its “open-weight” AI models as a tool for diplomacy, has promoted the technology as a global “public good” that should be managed by the international community. At a summit in India on Sunday, Xi offered the 11-member BRICS group of nations help developing open-source AI and urged them to join China’s global AI governance initiative.
But China is also keenly aware of the risks it faces from its own AI success, with Xi telling a Shanghai conference in July that authorities must “ensure that AI is always under human control.”

The industry must make mandatory filings and submit security assessments to officials, with many of the companies having to submit technical filings to an algorithm registry. The government has also imposed rules requiring watermarking and safety requirements.

Foremost among the risks are potential threats to China’s ruling Communist Party, which worries the technology could be weaponized against it and has imposed ideological controls to ensure products fall in line with socialist values, for example.

“Hostile forces and individuals with ulterior motives misuse generative AI technologies — such as deepfake audio-video, AI-generated graphics and text, and intelligent bot farms — to manufacture political rumors, spread harmful information, and incite confrontation at low cost and on a massive scale,” Chen Yixin, the Chinese minister of state security, said in an article Sunday in the state-backed China Cybersecurity Magazine that called for greater party control and government oversight of AI.

Chen said AI could enable misinformation campaigns and cyberattacks on China’s critical infrastructure and, in an apparent reference to the U.S., warned that countries with “advantages” in AI could restrict other nations’ access to their technologies.

He also warned of espionage and data leaks, days after Anthropic released a report that found Chinese AI labs had secretly routed requests to its Claude models, some of which contained sensitive information from individuals, major companies and state-affiliated actors.

Like the U.S., China increasingly views AI as a national security issue, down to the individual researchers working on it. On Tuesday, China tightened travel curbs on its citizens, barring some whose work has implications for national technology security from leaving the country.

The new rules add to an extensive AI regulatory regime that includes restrictions on AI companions over mental health concerns, mandated labeling of AI-generated content and a requirement that trained models must use data conforming to Chinese values.

Experts say it could take a major crisis for the U.S. and China to finally work together on AI, much like the 1962 Cuban missile crisis pushed the U.S. and the then-Soviet Union to start negotiating on nuclear weapons.

AI has already had profound military implications, including for targeting, and could be integrated into systems supporting the nuclear chain of command, said David Finkelstein, vice president of the Center for Naval Analyses.
“This is scary stuff, and I think that this is an area where the two sides ought to be sitting down and talking to each other,” he said at the forum.

U.S.-China competition is inevitable, but there is still room for the two sides to negotiate because their respective positions “are not necessarily very much entrenched,” said David Santoro, president and chief executive of Pacific Forum International, a Honolulu-based think tank.
“There are still ways that we can better understand each other and hopefully come up with mechanisms so we can better control this emerging technology,” he said in an interview at the forum.
Santoro said he was “not very optimistic,” however, about the prospect for a major agreement in the near term.
“I don’t know that we will be able to get to a position where we agree on something substantive,” he said. “But at least the first step has got to be talking to each other.”
Eric Baculinao and Erin Tan reported from Beijing and Mithil Aggarwal from Hong Kong.

title: Russia and Ukraine launch new energy attacks despite Trump’s ceasefire claim
summary: President Donald Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop striking each other’s energy infrastructure.
story: President Donald Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop striking each other’s energy infrastructure. Then overnight into Tuesday, both sides launched new energy attacks.

Russia fired a volley of 200 drones at Ukraine, hitting energy and port facilities, Ukrainian officials said. In the capital, Kyiv, one person was killed and seven others injured in attacks on two gas stations, warehouses and other sites, according to local authorities.
In the south and west, Russian strikes damaged homes, as well as port and transportation infrastructure.

Kyiv’s military meanwhile said it struck the Syzran oil refinery in Russia’s Samara region. Ukrainian officials also reported strikes on a drone production facility in Taganrog and a drone preparation and launch site in the Oryol region.
This is the daily reality of Russia’s assault, now into its fifth year, to bomb Ukraine’s military and population into submission.

title: Air Force officer recalls ‘free-falling’ after jet was shot down over Iran
summary: In an interview with CBS’ “60 Minutes,” one of the two U.S. Air Force officers whose fighter jet was shot down over Iran in April detailed his harrowing ordeal.
story: In an interview with CBS’ “60 Minutes” that aired Sunday, one of the two U.S. Air Force officers whose fighter jet was shot down over Iran in April detailed his harrowing ordeal, including plummeting to the ground with a damaged parachute.

The Defense Department has not identified the Air Force colonel by name. “60 Minutes” correspondent Norah O’Donnell said the show agreed to refer to the weapons systems officer by his mission call sign, “Bravo,” because of security threats from the Iranian regime.

In the interview, the lead segment on the 59th season premiere of the CBS newsmagazine, Bravo said he felt like he had been “hit by a freight train” when a shoulder-fired missile rammed into his F-15E two-seat fighter jet on April 2. The other Air Force officer hit the eject button.
“I will be thankful to my dying day for my pilot and crewmate, Alpha, for saving our lives and ejecting us,” Bravo told O’Donnell.

Bravo said he started “free-falling” toward a rugged mountainous area. He looked up and saw that his parachute had been damaged in the missile attack — a realization he called “the most terrifying thing I’ve ever seen.” Military professionals estimate he hit the Iranian desert somewhere between 70 and 100 mph, he said, adding that his survival was a “modern-day miracle.”

“60 Minutes” reported that the fall broke Bravo’s back, arm and shoulder, yet he managed to hike and climb a 7,000-foot ridgeline to evade capture. He was stranded behind enemy lines for two days without food or water before two elite Air Force pararescue operators got him out of harm’s way.

“Let’s go,” Bravo said he told his rescuers. “60 Minutes” characterized the search-and-rescue operation as one of the most complex and risky in U.S. military history. (Sunday’s segment did not feature an interview with Alpha, who landed 5 miles away from Bravo after they ejected from the F-15E.)
“60 Minutes” returned to the airwaves Sunday after a summer of turmoil at America’s leading broadcast newsmagazine.

CBS News Editor in Chief Bari Weiss undertook a sweeping shake-up at the show in late May. She tapped technology journalist and documentarian Nick Bilton as the program’s new executive producer, cut ties with a group of senior leaders and let go of two correspondents, Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi.

Scott Pelley, a veteran correspondent, excoriated Bilton at a June 1 staff meeting, questioning his qualifications for his role and objecting to the ousters of Vega and Alfonsi. Pelley was fired the next day. Alfonsi had previously clashed with Weiss over a segment about the Trump administration’s deportation of Venezuelan men to a prison in El Salvador.

Weiss and Bilton have since hired new on-air talent, including Ross Douthat, a former opinion columnist at The New York Times who is now a “60 Minutes” correspondent, and Sebastian Junger, a reporter and author who became a contributor to the series. Bilton announced in late July that O’Donnell had been elevated to full-time correspondent.

Sunday’s season premiere offered a glimpse of the revamped program, with slight adjustments to its on-air graphics. The two other segments that aired Sunday were an investigation into “brokers” paid to seek pardons from the Trump administration and an inside look at the Los Angeles Rams football franchise.
In the episode’s final minute, Douthat said “60 Minutes” was planning stories about the artificial intelligence boom.

“We may have a narrow window — this year, not the next 10 — to make artificial intelligence safe for humanity. That clock is ticking, and so is ours,” Douthat said, accompanied by the show’s signature “tick-tick-tick” sound effect. “For almost 60 years, it has meant the same thing: journalism you can trust. Where we’re headed, we’re going to need it.”

title: Harry and Meghan change their children’s school over security concerns
summary: Archie and Lilibet, the children of Harry and Meghan, have changed school just days after starting, following security concerns about transporting them.
story: LONDON — The children of Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, have changed school just days into the new academic year, with the couple citing security concerns.
Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, were enrolled in an undisclosed school when their parents moved back to Britain from California last month.
But just days after they started at the new school, they have now switched to another.

“The decision for the children to move school was taken following a discussion with the family’s security team about the practicalities of their current arrangements,” a spokesman for Harry and Meghan said in a statement.

“The parents remain extremely grateful to all the teachers and staff for the love, care and effort they have shown their family,” the statement added. “This decision should in no way be interpreted as a reflection on the school or the exceptional care the children have received there.”
HELLO! Magazine first reported the story.
NBC News royal contributor Emily Nash cited specific concerns the couple appeared to have.

The school “was at a fair distance from the place where they’re staying in the U.K. and they weren’t able to properly protect themselves in heavy traffic,” Nash, who is also royal editor for HELLO! Magazine, said in an interview.
“On the first day of term, they realized it was going to be quite a challenging journey for them and they risked sitting in traffic where they were potentially exposed to greater threats,”she said.
The news comes as the couple await a verdict on their request for publicly-funded security protection.
A government committee was due to review whether to provide security for the couple now that their living arrangements in the United Kingdom are more permanent.

The location of their new home has not been disclosed and questions remain over what arrangements will be in place given the protracted legal battle between Harry and the British government over the issue.
The family moved back to the United Kingdom for an “extended period” of time after six years living in Montecito, California.
Their decision to “step back” from frontline royal duties and leave the U.K. in 2020 sent shock waves around the world.
Since then, royal relations have been publicly strained, with allegations of racism and bullying made by the couple in their Netflix documentary “Harry & Meghan” and in Harry’s memoir, “Spare.”

There were new signs of strain last week, when the couple indicated they had been left “surprised” by a letter on behalf of King Charles III that reiterated they would remain private individuals and nonworking members of the royal family during their renewed stint in the U.K.
Earlier this week, Meghan shared online a series of family photos of their new life in England, showcasing her children fishing on a boat, riding bikes and taking woodland walks with their dog.
On Tuesday morning, she paid tribute to her husband on his 42nd birthday, saying that he was “simply the best.”

title: How Ukraine’s futuristic war could get ‘much worse,’ according to ex-Google CEO
summary: “The rate of innovation is faster than I’ve ever seen, and I work in tech,” Eric Schmidt told NBC News’ Richard Engel.
story: Ukraine’s battlefield “kill zones,” where leaving your bunker can mean death by Russian drone within minutes, look set to grow swiftly as the war drives breathtaking technological advancements, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt has warned.

Schmidt, now CEO and executive chairman of rocket maker Relativity Space, is helping Ukraine fight a technological battle with the Kremlin that moves so quickly that weapons can lose their advantage within months.

“The rate of innovation is faster than I’ve ever seen, and I work in tech,” Schmidt told Richard Engel, NBC News’ chief foreign correspondent. Schmidt previously chaired the U.S. National Security Commission on Artificial Intelligence and has advised the Pentagon.
As Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine stretches into its fifth year, Schmidt said Moscow is becoming better at developing and deploying new weapons, eroding an advantage Ukraine had relied on.

“Historically, Ukraine was this small, really smart, really fast innovator, and the Russians were, if you will, big, slow, not very capable. That’s changed,” he said in an interview for the weekly global affairs podcast “The World with Richard Engel and Yalda Hakim.”

The conflict has become a testing ground for drone warfare and thus the place for some of the technology’s latest advancements. From the Ukrainian towns now covered in anti-drone netting to the sites deep inside Russia vulnerable to attack from Kyiv, drones have become the war’s defining weapon.
President Donald Trump, who during his election campaign promised to resolve the conflict in 24 hours, has repeatedly pressured Ukraine to cede key territory and favored Moscow’s hard-line demands.
Winning would depend on how quickly either side could get its latest inventions into widespread use, Schmidt argued.
“Whoever plays the game of fastest innovation to scale will win this war,” he said.
